observed_text: Loss of phase coherence across the loop removes the oscillation; in gold rings its amplitude depends on temperature.
implied_text: Clock is path coherence, not a plasma period.
description: Loss of phase coherence collapses the AB shift.
notes: No coherence length or time is filed.

observed_text: The fundamental period in a normal conductor is h/e. Normal-metal rings also show a weaker h/2e component, and the shielded-toroid experiment used a superconductor whose own flux is quantized.
implied_text: Do not fold AB into gapped-condensate or identify the two quanta.
description: h/e versus h/2e is a load-bearing distinction, but both periods can appear in one apparatus.

observed_text: Fringe shift or resistance oscillation periodic in Φ_AB = h/e = 4.135667696e-15 Wb (exact). One period for a 1 µm diameter loop is 5.3 mT.
implied_text: Single-charge flux period, not superconducting h/2e.
description: The stable output is an h/e-periodic phase shift.
notes: Twice the tabulated flux quantum h/2e. Contrast with flux-quantization Φ0=h/2e.

observed_text: Enclosed flux sets a phase, Δφ = qΦ/ħ. There is no static barrier holding a latched state.
implied_text: Driven interferometer, not a memory.
description: AB is not a latch.
value_text: no latch; Φ writes a phase

observed_text: A path that does not encircle the flux, or Φ→0, removes the shift.
implied_text: Topology / zero flux is the collapse of this effect.
description: No enclosed flux ⇒ no AB shift.
notes: Topology is a threshold. The dependence on Φ itself is continuous: phase linear in Φ, pattern periodic in h/e.

observed_text: Two coherent paths that together enclose a flux. A toroidal magnet shielded by superconductor and copper gave a measured phase shift between a beam through the hole and a beam outside. Submicron gold rings show the same period in their resistance.
implied_text: The loop is the buffer. The solenoid interior is not the electron's hardware.
description: AB needs a multiply connected coherent path around a confined flux.
notes: In a metal ring the field also passes through the metal; the field-free condition belongs to the electron-beam experiment.

observed_text: Antiferromagnetic resonance at low temperature: MnF2 261.4 GHz, MnO 0.82 THz, NiO 1.10 THz, FeF2 1.58 THz. It scales as √(2·HE·HA). kTN/h is 2.5 THz (MnO) and 10.9 THz (NiO).
implied_text: The clock is exchange and anisotropy together: two to three orders above ferromagnetic resonance and well below kTN/h. There is no slow AFM write unless a spin-flop field or an exchange-bias field-cool is imposed.
description: The antiferromagnetic clock is the sub-THz to THz resonance, not kTN/h and not the 28 GHz/T ferromagnetic carrier.
notes: value_si is NiO. The first version said the rate was set by kTN; the measured resonance is 0.10–0.33 of kTN/h.

observed_text: The mapping takes the sign of the inter-sublattice coupling as data (the lattice and electronic structure that make J antiferromagnetic).
implied_text: QSA does not here derive why MnO is AFM and Fe is FM. That is a gap in the node rules, not a gap in the latch accounting.
description: The AFM sign of J is taken, not produced from a more primitive node rule.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Weak ferromagnetism/canting is not this gap.

observed_text: Mnet ≈ 0 on the scale of a ferromagnet of the same sublattice magnetization. The sample exerts no useful permanent-magnet force.
implied_text: Cancelled net moment / ~0 force is the stable output of two opposed latches, not evidence that nothing is latched.
description: The cancelled latch emits approximately zero macroscopic force while the neutron superlattice remains.
notes: Weak canting in some compounds is a small remainder (hematite about 0.4 A m²/kg); it does not convert the family into the permanent-magnet latch.

observed_text: Holding the ordered (cancelled) state costs zero continuous power. There is no hysteresis-heat bill at rest.
implied_text: A static antiparallel superlattice with Mnet ≈ 0, held at zero continuous power below TN.
description: Holding the cancelled latch costs zero watts.

observed_text: Exchange holds the sublattices antiparallel; anisotropy fixes the axis. The Curie–Weiss temperature θ is 1.1 to 5.3 times TN in the monoxides (MnO 610/116, FeO 570/198, CoO 330/291, NiO ≈2000/525).
implied_text: Two energy scales, not one. A single exchange number does not give both θ and TN. The emergent dipole is ~0 because the sublattices are opposed; cancelled force is the output, not a failure.
description: A latch is a held configuration at zero hold-power, not a requirement of a nonzero dipole.
notes: θ is a Curie–Weiss fit parameter and depends on the fitted window. θ = TN only in the nearest-neighbour two-sublattice mean-field model.

observed_text: Néel temperatures: MnO 118 K (sources 116–120), FeO 198 K (183–200, stoichiometry-dependent), CoO 291 K, NiO 523 K (520–525). Above TN the magnetic reflections are gone and the material is an ordinary paramagnet.
implied_text: Thermal loss of sublattice order → magnetic Bragg intensity gone, Curie–Weiss paramagnet.
description: The cancelled latch dies at TN, the analog of a ferromagnetic Curie point.
notes: A continuous phase transition: sharp in a large crystal, rounded and shifted in thin layers.

observed_text: Spin-flop fields in uniaxial crystals: MnF2 9.3 T, Cr2O3 6.0 T, FeF2 41.9 T; CoO 7.0 T at 240 K. For cubic NiO only 0.24 T (in-plane, computed) and 1.54 T (second-hand) were found; nothing for MnO.
implied_text: A spin-flop field is a field write of the sublattice orientation, not everyday ferromagnetic coercivity. It is a clean threshold only in uniaxial crystals.
description: Fields of 6–42 T rotate the sublattices of uniaxial antiferromagnets; the cubic monoxides show no single clean spin-flop.
notes: value_si is MnF2. The first version claimed tesla-class spin-flop fields for the monoxides without a source.

observed_text: Neutron diffraction on MnO at 80 K shows magnetic reflections that are absent at room temperature, from a magnetic cell twice the chemical cell. Two-sublattice accounting: MA ≈ −MB, so Mnet ≈ 0. A single spin is not an antiferromagnet.
implied_text: Hardware is two (or more) interpenetrating sublattices, each a directional latch, correlated over a volume large enough that exchange holds the antiparallel relation against kT.
description: The cancelled latch requires at least two opposed ordered populations, not a single-moment cell.
notes: Readable hardware is the magnetic superlattice (neutron or electron diffraction, resonance), not a dipole field. Size effects are a crossover with no portable length.

observed_text: kT/h = 6.25 THz at 300 K, with h and k exact. Below it the spectrum follows the Rayleigh–Jeans form; above it the spectrum falls as ν³exp(−hν/kT).
implied_text: Frequencies well below kT/h sit in the Rayleigh–Jeans envelope; frequencies well above it are exponentially empty. A wall that has not finished exchanging does not emit a single-T spectrum.
description: The spectral clock is the defined ratio kT/h plus the wall exchange window.
notes: h and k are defined. 6.25 THz is arithmetic at 300 K, not an extracted machine clock.

observed_text: The mapping does not derive h or the Planck occupation factor. A sub-wavelength emitter departs from the black-body law, which confirms that size against λ_max is the buffer without supplying a universal volume.
implied_text: QSA takes the measured curve and the Wien product as the output specification. Mode count is the buffer; those corrections confirm that without supplying a single universal volume.
description: h is taken, not derived, and there is no universal cavity volume. That is the same honest limit as the missing N on the temperature entry.
value_text: h taken; no universal cavity volume
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: A black cavity emits the Planck spectrum, depending only on T, with λ_max T = 2.897772e-3 m·K. The cosmic microwave background measured by FIRAS deviates from a black body by less than 50 ppm of the peak (rms) at T = 2.72548 ± 0.00057 K.
implied_text: The Planck curve u(ν,T) and its Wien peak, depending only on T, are the averaged spectral output of the thermal electromagnetic population.
description: The machine’s stable product is the measured Planck shape, not a derived occupation factor.
notes: h and k are exact. Rayleigh–Jeans is the low-frequency limit and diverges if extended. Integral owned by stefan-boltzmann.

observed_text: A polished metal is not black: total emissivity at 300 K is 0.05 for polished aluminium and 0.10 for polished copper, against 0.94 for black paint.
implied_text: That is a failure of the black-body boundary condition, not a stored state.
description: The blackbody spectrum has an operating boundary condition (ε=1), not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
notes: Cross-cite plasma-frequency-cutoff and reflection for why a metal wall is not black in the optical.

observed_text: An emitter thinner than the thermal wavelength leaves the black-body law: a 500 nm silica fibre radiates with a power rising more slowly than T³ and agrees with a volume-emission (fluctuational electrodynamics) model.
implied_text: As the emitter falls below λ_max(T) the smooth black-body output is lost continuously.
description: Sub-wavelength emitters fail the Planck output.
notes: Crossover on the scale λ_max(T). Discrete few-mode cavity spectra were not sourced.

observed_text: Emission scales with emissivity: total emissivity at 300 K is 0.94 for black paint, 0.05 for polished aluminium, 0.10 for polished copper, 0.17 for polished stainless steel.
implied_text: The wall has failed the black boundary condition. The same metal can succeed as a mirror and fail as a blackbody.
description: Non-black surfaces do not emit the universal Planck curve.
value_text: ε < 1 (0.05–0.17 for polished metals at 300 K)
notes: Photoemission from the same hot wall is a different machine (photoelectric-threshold, work-function-thermionic).

observed_text: If the wall population itself has no stable T — too few contributors, or observation inside its exchange window — there is no thermal spectrum to emit.
implied_text: The spectrum inherits the temperature entry’s collapse: no stable wall average, no Planck curve.
description: An undefined wall T removes the thermal electromagnetic output.
value_text: wall T not a stable average
notes: Inherited crossover (N^{-1/2} scatter, exchange window). Cross-cite thermal-equilibrium-temperature.

observed_text: The energy is carried near λ_max = 2898 µm·K / T: 9.66 µm at 300 K, 1.06 mm at 2.725 K. A silica fibre 500 nm in diameter, thinner than the thermal wavelength, does not follow the black-body law: its radiated power rises more slowly than T³.
implied_text: The emitter or cavity must be large compared with the wavelengths that carry the energy at that T; the scale tracks λ_max(T) and there is no universal volume.
description: The hardware is a thermal electromagnetic population over a dense mode set, coupled to a wall with a stable T. No universal volume is extracted.
notes: The few-mode cavity picture of the first version has no opened source; the measured case is a sub-wavelength emitter.

observed_text: Trap frequencies set the sloshing / expansion clocks of the cloud; they are apparatus scales, not a universal condensate clock. There is no Josephson 2e/h lock and no cyclotron clock. Interaction-driven sound in the condensed cloud is a hydrodynamic response of an already-formed condensate.
implied_text: The BEC has no metrological lock and no material gap frequency; its clocks are trap and hydro scales of an already condensed cloud.
description: Laboratory BEC clocks are apparatus and hydro, not a universal condensate tick.
notes: Analogous to second sound on superfluid-helium-4.

observed_text: An ideal-gas BEC has no measured pairing gap. Collapse is loss of macroscopic occupation and of phase coherence, not gap closure of the superconducting kind. N ~ 10^3–10^7 is a working envelope, not a derived minimum node count. The laboratory condensate is not held at zero continuous power.
implied_text: The file sits in gapped-coherence because the taxonomy groups protected collective modes that die at a critical temperature. Forcing a gap onto the alkali cloud would be an interpretive overlay. QSA takes 2.612 from the ideal-gas condition.
description: Family assignment is looser than a pairing gap; the thermal/density threshold is real, the gap language is not, and the phase-space threshold is taken rather than derived.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this tension, the absence of a minimum node count, and the taken 2.612. A dilute condensate is a superfluid by direct test (critical velocity, persistent flow); dense 4He differs in density and interaction strength.

observed_text: A sharp peak on the thermal distribution, imaged after the trap is switched off, and interference between two condensates. A stirred condensate heats only above a critical velocity, and flow in a toroidal trap persists for up to 10 s.
implied_text: The stable output is a macroscopic occupation of one mode — read as a condensate fraction, a narrow velocity peak, and interference contrast — only while the cloud stays above the critical phase-space density.
description: The machine's product is one-mode occupation and interference contrast, not a quantized electrical constant.
notes: No claim is made about what the condensate is. Relation to superfluid-helium-4 is analogical.

observed_text: The condensate fraction, 1 − (T/Tc)³ in a harmonic trap, falls to zero at Tc, or as the density is lowered through n λT³ = 2.612 at fixed T. This is not an anisotropy barrier and not a pairing gap.
implied_text: The load-bearing threshold is thermal / density. Holding the condensate requires continuous cooling and trapping resources; it is not a zero-power latch.
description: BEC is gated by Tc(n), not by a pairing gap or a remanence barrier.
value_text: T > Tc(n) or n dropped at fixed T
notes: Contrast with permanent-magnet-latch and flux-quantization, which hold state at zero continuous power.

observed_text: Above Tc(n) the condensate fraction, 1 − (T/Tc)³ in a harmonic trap, is zero; a sudden onset is measured at T/Tc ≈ 1.
implied_text: T > Tc(n) destroys macroscopic occupation and phase coherence.
description: Thermal collapse of the condensate fraction at the density-set Tc.
notes: Working Tc sits in the nK–μK class of the apparatus envelope. Heating and three-body loss are practical routes to this collapse, not a third machine class.

observed_text: The condition n λT³ = 2.612 can be crossed by lowering the density at fixed temperature. When the trap is switched off the cloud expands; the narrow peak and the interference fringes are imaged during that expansion, which also ends the sample.
implied_text: Atom loss or a weaker trap lowers n through the critical line at fixed T, the same collapse as warming. Without confinement the cloud is not a lasting laboratory condensate, although release is also the readout step.
description: A fall in density walks the cloud back through nλT³ ≈ 2.612.
notes: Same critical line as the hardware-scale row; this row is the density-drop failure.

observed_text: Ideal-gas threshold n λT³ = ζ(3/2) ≃ 2.612 at the centre of the trap; kTc = 0.94 ħω N^(1/3). The measured transition is very close to this value. Sodium at 2 μK needs 1.5×10¹⁴ cm⁻³, as measured.
implied_text: The nodes are the atoms; the buffer is the combination of number, volume, and temperature that puts enough of them in one mode. This is the measured phase-space condition taken as the specification, not a derived node rule.
description: A trapped cloud becomes a condensate when its phase-space density crosses the ideal-gas value 2.612.
notes: Envelope/relabel of the ideal-gas condition, not a derived node rule. In a harmonic trap the same condition at peak density gives Tc that scales as N^{1/3} times the trap frequency.

observed_text: Atom numbers range from a few thousand to several million; about 300 nK for 40,000 atoms; sodium condensates of up to 5×10⁵ atoms below about 2 μK.
implied_text: A working envelope of the apparatus class. There is no minimum atom number at which the effect switches on; the transition is rounded in a finite system.
description: The laboratory node count is a working envelope, not a derived minimum.
notes: value_si is a geometric mid-class of the quoted atom-number window. Species-by-species scattering lengths and interaction Tc shifts are medium and are not required here.

observed_text: Momentum relaxation τ_p = m/γ is 55 ns for a 1 µm sphere of density 1.0 g/cm³ in water at 20 °C. For t ≪ τ_p the motion is ballistic; for t ≫ τ_p ⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt per axis.
implied_text: Two clocks: bath collision time, and tracer velocity-forget time τ_p. The overdamped MSD law is a clock constraint, not a different effect.
description: The overdamped Einstein walk applies only after the tracer has forgotten its momentum.
value_text: τ_p = 55 ns (1 µm sphere in water)
notes: Density assumed. In a liquid hydrodynamic memory modifies the simple τ_p.

observed_text: The mapping does not derive k or the Stokes coefficient. D scales continuously as 1/a; there is no particle-size threshold.
implied_text: QSA takes D = kT/γ and the measured τ_p crossover as the specifications. The missing universal radius is the same statistical gap as the missing N on the temperature entry.
description: k and the Stokes prefactor are taken; no universal tracer size is extracted.
value_text: k and 6π taken; no universal a
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: D = kT/γ and ⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt per axis for t ≫ τ_p. A 1 µm sphere in water at 20 °C has D = 4.3e-13 m²/s, 0.93 µm rms per axis in one second.
implied_text: Diffusivity and a linearly growing MSD are the still-visible remainder of an incomplete impact average. For large bodies the emergent output on the same window is stillness.
description: The named output is the Einstein relation; its electrical counterpart is 4kTRΔf.
notes: k is exact. 4.3e-13 m²/s is the value for one tracer and bath, not a machine number.

observed_text: D = kT/γ: the motion scales with kT against the drag and involves no barrier.
implied_text: Jitter is not a stored configuration.
description: Brownian motion has no energy barrier that stores a state.
notes: k is exact.

observed_text: D = kT/6πηa falls as 1/a: rms displacement per axis in one second is 0.93 µm for a 1 µm sphere in water and 29 nm for a 1 mm sphere.
implied_text: This is completion of the average — collapse of the visible effect, not a missing machine.
description: When the impact average finishes inside the observation window, the named jitter disappears and the object looks still.
notes: Crossover in 1/a. This is completion of the average, not a missing machine.

observed_text: For t ≪ τ_p the motion is ballistic, ⟨x²⟩ ≈ kTt²/m; the full Langevin form joins it to 2Dt. The ballistic regime has been measured for one particle in a liquid with 75 MHz bandwidth.
implied_text: Clock constraint on the overdamped output, not a different machine.
description: Observe faster than momentum relaxation and the Einstein walk is the wrong envelope.
notes: Crossover at τ_p. Knudsen conditions separately fail Stokes drag.

observed_text: D = kT/γ falls continuously with T (and with rising viscosity).
implied_text: Shrink the thermal resource and the incomplete mechanical average disappears.
description: No thermal bath energy, no Einstein diffusivity.
notes: Shares this collapse with johnson-nyquist-noise (4kTRΔf).

observed_text: D = kT/6πηa falls as 1/a: a 1 µm sphere in water at 20 °C has D = 4.3e-13 m²/s (0.93 µm rms per axis in 1 s); a 1 mm sphere has D = 4.3e-16 m²/s (29 nm). Stokes drag holds for laminar flow at Reynolds number below 1.
implied_text: Everyday stillness is the completed average; Brownian motion is the under-averaged remainder. “Visible” tracks optical resolution, T, η, and the chosen window.
description: No universal particle size is extracted. Making the tracer larger completes the average; D falls continuously as 1/a.
value_text: no universal radius; bath continuum (L ≳ λ)
notes: No universal radius: D scales continuously as 1/a and 'visible' is set by resolution.

observed_text: Characteristic frequency c/2d: ħc/2d is 0.99 eV at 100 nm and 0.10 eV at 1 µm. The force integrates the response of the faces over a wide band around it.
implied_text: Clock is the gap electromagnetic spectrum, far below the plasma edge of the faces.
description: Mode spectrum of the gap, not ωp of the faces.

observed_text: The π²ħc/240 prefactor is taken from the mode sum. Real faces reduce the force through their measured dielectric response; roughness and patch potentials also sit between the formula and any one apparatus.
implied_text: Same class of taken output as the optical decay length λ/4πk.
description: Prefactor taken; mapping Medium.

observed_text: Ideal plate pressure π²ħc/240d⁴ = 1.30 mPa at d = 1 µm (K_C = 1.300e-27 N m²). Measured K_C = (1.22 ± 0.18)e-27 N m² at 0.5–3.0 µm. Thick real metals give 0.48–0.55 of the ideal force at 0.1 µm.
implied_text: Taken mode-sum output, not derived from a node count; real faces reduce it continuously.
description: The stable output is the Casimir/Lifshitz attraction.
notes: value_si is the ideal 1 µm plate pressure.

observed_text: The force is a geometry output of the mode spectrum. No stored bit.
implied_text: Not a latch.
description: Casimir is not a memory.

observed_text: The ideal force falls as 1/d⁴ for plates and 1/d³ for a sphere and plate. It has been measured out to 6–7 µm; above about 3 µm at 300 K the thermal contribution dominates.
implied_text: Opening the gap lowers the output continuously.
description: A power law in d with no critical gap.
notes: value_si is the largest gap at which the force has been measured; there is no critical gap.

observed_text: Measured from about 50 nm to 7 µm: 0.1–0.9 µm (atomic force microscope), 0.5–3.0 µm (parallel plates), 0.6–6 µm and 0.7–7 µm (torsion). A 9 nm palladium film and a visibly transparent conducting oxide still give a force.
implied_text: The buffer is the gap (which electromagnetic modes fit). The faces need an electromagnetic contrast; no minimum face thickness is measured.
description: Casimir needs a sub-micrometre to micrometre gap between contrasting faces.
notes: The first version required conducting faces thicker than their screening depth; withdrawn. value_si is the 1 µm class.

observed_text: No interaction time was sourced.
implied_text: Detector integration is collection.
description: Interaction time not sourced.

observed_text: The recoil threshold is an instrument floor: the maximum recoil is 96 eV for a 1.8 MeV neutrino on germanium, against a 160 eV detector threshold. The weak coupling and the form factor are taken.
implied_text: Do not treat the calorimeter floor as the process gate.
description: Detection floor is not the process gate. Mapping Medium.
notes: No opened measurement uses neutrinos below 1.8 MeV.

observed_text: CsI: 134 ± 22 events, 6.7 σ. Argon: flux-averaged cross section (2.2 ± 0.7)e-39 cm². Reactor antineutrinos on germanium: 395 ± 106 events, 3.7 σ.
implied_text: N² recoils as the synchronized output of many νA events.
description: Coherent N² recoil rate.

observed_text: The interaction has no energy threshold. Coherence requires qR < 1: full below about 10 MeV, partial at the 16–53 MeV of the spallation-source measurement. Inverse beta decay, a different channel, opens at 1.806 MeV.
implied_text: The gate is the coherence window, not a rest-mass threshold.
description: qR < 1 is the operating window; coherence is full below about 10 MeV.
notes: The first version put the spallation-source neutrinos inside qR ≪ 1.

observed_text: Coherence is lost gradually through the nuclear form factor as qR grows; the N² signal is still observed at 16–53 MeV with partial coherence. With no nucleus there is no recoil.
implied_text: Loss of coherence is a crossover, not under-threshold non-occurrence at a rest-mass gate.
description: Rising momentum transfer reduces coherence gradually; a missing nucleus removes the recoil.
value_text: qR ≳ 1: gradual loss; or no nucleus

observed_text: One neutrino and one nucleus. The interaction probability rises as N²: 6084 for ¹³³Cs, 484 for ⁴⁰Ar. Observed in CsI, argon and germanium.
implied_text: Same extra-node shape as pair production, different probe.
description: Hardware is ν + nucleus.

observed_text: The charging time is RtC: 0.1 ns for 100 kΩ and 1 fF.
implied_text: Observation faster than charging is not a blockade reading.
description: RC / tunnel clock.
notes: The first version wrote the clock as (e² RT C)⁻¹, which is not a rate.

observed_text: h/e² enters here as the scale of tunnel resistance above which the island charge is well defined. It is the same constant as the von Klitzing constant, 25 812.807 Ω, and is not a Hall plateau here.
implied_text: Do not identify with QHE RH.
description: Same combination h/e², different role.

observed_text: Conductance oscillations periodic in gate voltage with period e/Cg; current steps at bias intervals of about e/C (0.16 mV at 1 fF).
implied_text: Stable output is a blockaded window periodic in e.
description: Diamond / staircase as the gated output.

observed_text: Ec = e²/2C in one convention; the standard review uses e²/C. 80 µeV at 1 fF. Current is blocked inside a bias window of order e/C that is periodic in gate voltage.
implied_text: Ec is the load-bearing gate. Not φ and not a latch barrier.
description: Single-electron charging gate.

observed_text: Thermal fluctuations suppress charge quantization exponentially. Opening a channel suppresses it as the square root of the residual reflection, reaching zero at a ballistic contact (about 2e²/h). The conditions e²/C ≫ kT and Rt ≫ h/e² = 25 812.807 Ω are order-of-magnitude.
implied_text: Thermal overrun and loss of integer charge are crossovers with measured forms, not sharp collapses.
description: Raising T or opening the barriers reduces the blockade continuously.
value_text: e²/C ≫ kT; Rt ≫ h/e² (25.8 kΩ scale)

observed_text: For C = 1 fF, e²/2C is 80 µeV (k × 0.93 K); for 1 aF it is 80 meV. The first devices had about 1 fF or less; a 10 nm grain reaches 100 meV (as e²/C).
implied_text: The island is the buffer. A larger island has a larger C and a smaller gate, falling as 1/C.
description: Charging-energy buffer is the island capacitance.

observed_text: Single moments precess at 28.02 GHz/T (CODATA 2022). The Curie reading is a time average of the projection along the field. No relaxation time is filed.
implied_text: Observation faster than the bath exchange, or faster than the moment’s relaxation in the host, is not χ = C/T.
description: χ = C/T is an average over the host / bath relaxation window, not a single-spin precession readout.
notes: 28.025 GHz/T is the single-spin carrier owned as a clock by permanent-magnet-latch. Do not treat it as a Curie-law number.

observed_text: C and θ are taken from fits or from the ionic configuration; the mapping does not compute them and names no minimum spin count.
implied_text: C and θ are taken from measurement. Those are the same honest gaps as on the other ensemble-average entries.
description: C and θ are taken, not derived, and no universal moment count is extracted.
value_text: C, θ taken; no universal N
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. k is defined.

observed_text: χ = C/T, an experimental fit valid at high temperature and weak field, with C = μ0 n g² μ_B² J(J+1)/3k for non-interacting moments; C/(T − θ) with interactions. Zero remanence at zero field.
implied_text: Reversible susceptibility is the averaged projection of an unlocked-moment population. Remanence at B=0 is the latch, not this average.
description: The stable output is χ = C/T with zero remnant. That is the unlocked contrast to the latched magnet.
notes: Pauli paramagnetism of a metal goes to a constant at low temperature and is not filed as Curie.

observed_text: No barrier holds the moments: the magnetization curve of Cr³⁺ alum follows the reversible Brillouin function to 99.5 % of saturation, with no remanence at zero field.
implied_text: This machine exists only while there is no anisotropy barrier holding a remnant. Soft iron above its useful coercivity but below T_C is still a ferromagnetic collective, not Curie.
description: Curie paramagnetism requires the absence of the magnet-latch barrier.
value_text: no latch; unlocked moments; zero remnant at B=0
notes: Contrast with permanent-magnet-latch. Ferromagnetic-hysteresis owns the poorly latched ferromagnet. Superparamagnetism is a small grain with a KV barrier that only looks unlocked above T_B.

observed_text: χ = C/T falls without limit as T rises; the law itself holds at high temperature and weak field.
implied_text: High-T collapse of the useful moment is still Curie, just an unusably small average.
description: χ = C/T remains the envelope as T→∞, but the useful moment for a given B disappears.
notes: Continuous, 1/T. Not a change of family.

observed_text: Above the ordering temperature χ = C/(T − θ) (mean field); the form fails close to the Curie point, and below it the ferromagnet has a spontaneous magnetization.
implied_text: χ = C/T dies because the machine has changed family — unlocked ensemble replaced by latched or staggered order — not because this average was merely cooled.
description: Order at T_C / T_N / θ replaces the Curie ensemble with a different machine.
notes: A phase transition. Ordering temperatures are filed on the ordered-state entries.

observed_text: μ_B/k = 0.6717 K/T, so μ_B B = kT at 447 T (300 K) and 1.49 T (1 K). Cr³⁺ alum reaches 99.5 % of saturation at 1.29 K and 5 T, following the Brillouin function (99.6 % computed) and not the Langevin function. At 1 T and 300 K the same ion is at 0.37 % of saturation.
implied_text: Above μB ∼ kT the Brillouin function saturates and χ is no longer C/T.
description: Large B/T takes the unlocked population out of the linear Curie envelope without locking it.
value_text: M/M_sat = B_J(gμ_B J B/kT); 99.5 % at 5 T and 1.29 K
notes: A function of B/T with no critical field.

observed_text: A population of moments free to follow the field and sharing a bath temperature. χ is the averaged response; no minimum count is defined. One mole of S = 1/2, g = 2 moments has a Curie constant of 0.375 cm³ K/mol.
implied_text: Macro χ is the averaged response of the unlocked population. Dilute moments still follow Curie once N is large enough for the magnetometer; concentrated moments follow Curie–Weiss until they lock.
description: Curie paramagnetism is a statistical unlocked-moment average. No spin-count cliff and no KV volume threshold are extracted.
value_text: no universal N; volume is count, not KV
notes: Contrast with permanent-magnet-latch and superparamagnetism (a grain with a KV barrier and a retention-time crossover).

observed_text: ωc = eB/m*. Free electron: fc/B = 27.99 GHz T^{-1}. GaAs conduction electrons: m* = 0.067 m0, so 0.42 THz T^{-1}. In a two-dimensional sheet the collective line is at ω² = ωp² + ωc².
implied_text: Clock is load-bearing. ω must match ωc. B sets that clock. τ is the reset / decoherence time of the orbital motion.
description: A driven orbital clock at eB/m*, not a plasma-period screening cycle.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency. The spin-resonance value is 28.025 GHz T^{-1}, 0.116 % higher; the two lines are distinct and the degree of freedom here is orbital. Ge transverse 0.34 and Si transverse 0.15 THz T^{-1}.

observed_text: The mapping records 0.067 m0 in GaAs as a measured output of the lattice-plus-carrier machine. It does not derive that fraction from node rules.
implied_text: m* is located as an emergent output. The lattice that renormalizes the mass is pointed at, not derived here.
description: Open item is m* itself. Clock match and the ωc τ condition still close as a High mapping.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. CR does not become a lattice-mode entry: the collapse is not a phonon cutoff. Cross-cite semiconductor-gap-absorption and faraday-rotation (off-resonant cousin).

observed_text: The resonance field at a known frequency is read as an effective mass. GaAs electrons: m* = 0.067 m0. Ge electrons near 4 K: ml = 1.58, mt = 0.082; Si: ml = 0.97, mt = 0.19 (units of the electron mass).
implied_text: An absorption line whose position is the effective mass (or mass tensor) of the carrier population.
description: The synchronized orbital response emits m* as a measured output, not as a derived node mass.
notes: value_si left null: the file quotes ratios to the electron mass. In a two-dimensional sheet the collective line is shifted by the plasma term and must be corrected before it is read as a mass.

observed_text: No continuous power is required of the sample beyond the probing field. B sets ωc and raises ωc τ.
implied_text: No latch. field-threshold marks B as a clock-setting resource, not a stored-state barrier.
description: CR is a driven orbital match. There is no barrier holding a written state.

observed_text: Off resonance the absorption falls along a line of width about 1/τ. Only one sense of circular polarization is absorbed.
implied_text: Clock mismatch lowers the absorption continuously over the linewidth.
description: The load-bearing spectral failure is detuning from ωc.
notes: B→0 sends ωc→0 and ωcτ→0 together.

observed_text: With too much scattering the line is not resolved at the matching field. The condition is ωc τ = μB ≫ 1; it is met at 295 K above 100 T in a film with mobility 100 cm² V^{-1} s^{-1} (μB = 1 at 100 T).
implied_text: The orbit is not completed. Temperature acts by shortening τ, and a higher field compensates.
description: Scattering-time failure of the orbital clock. Twin of the ωcτ≳1 hardware spec.
notes: A crossover in μB, not a transition temperature. quantum-hall-effect uses the same high-μB two-dimensional carriers; the output there is a quantized Hall resistance, not an m* line.

observed_text: A well-resolved line needs ωc τ ≫ 1, equivalently μB ≫ 1. ωc τ = 1 at 1 T needs τ = 5.7 ps (free electron) or 0.38 ps (GaAs), i.e. a mobility of 10⁴ cm² V^{-1} s^{-1}.
implied_text: The quantity that gates the line is the scattering time against the orbit period — a clock resource. No film-thickness specification.
description: Hardware is a carrier population whose scattering time lets an orbit be a well-defined clock.
notes: Si/Ge resonances were recorded near 4 K, but low temperature is one route only: a 100 cm²/(V s) film gives a resolved line above 100 T, one at 295 K.

observed_text: In metals the line is seen below the plasma frequency with B parallel to the surface. The field occupies a thin skin layer; carriers accelerated there orbit in the bulk and return to the layer in step with the drive (Azbel'–Kaner resonance).
implied_text: 3D-metal CR adds the skin layer as the only volume the drive occupies. The cyclotron match is a different clock from the skin itself.
description: Metal CR borrows skin-effect’s screening length as its spatial buffer.
value_text: Azbel–Kaner recut of the skin layer
notes: Cross-cite skin-effect.

observed_text: Debye temperatures: Pb 105 K (0 K limit) and 87 K (298 K fit); Si 640 K; diamond 1860 K. Debye frequency kΘ_D/h: 2.2 THz (Pb), 13.3 THz (Si), 38.8 THz (diamond).
implied_text: ω_D is the clock ceiling of the ion grid under the linear-spectrum count. Below it only a T³-growing fraction of the 3N modes is in play; above it the mechanical spectrum is fully occupied.
description: The Debye clock runs from 2.2 THz (Pb) to 38.8 THz (diamond), a fitted stand-in for the top of the measured spectrum.
notes: value_si is the Pb value. The measured top of the spectrum lies above ν_D in Si (15.5 THz) and diamond (39.9 THz).

observed_text: Placing the ceiling at one spherical ω_D is an interpolation: the measured top branch lies above ν_D in Si and diamond. QSA takes fitted Θ_D as the clock specification and does not derive it.
implied_text: The 3N ceiling is tight; the Debye-sphere pin is taken, not derived.
description: Finite mode count is closed. A single spherical Θ_D is an interpolation over the real zone boundary.
value_text: Θ_D taken; sphere vs zone boundary
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Gap is the sphere versus the real zone boundary, not the existence of a cutoff.

observed_text: Θ_D: Pb 105 K (0 K) and 87 K (298 K); Si 640 K; diamond 1860 K. Heat capacity as a fraction of the Dulong–Petit value near room temperature: Pb 1.08, Si 0.79, diamond 0.25. Low-T insulator heat capacity follows T³; metals add γT.
implied_text: A material-typical Θ_D and the two heat-capacity limits it organizes are the averaged output of a finite, synchronized mechanical population.
description: The finite-mode machine emits a Θ_D from about 100 K (Pb) to 1860 K (diamond), with T³ and 3Nk as the organized limits.
notes: Any one Θ_D is medium: it depends on fit method and temperature. Metals add a γT term owned by electron-heat-capacity.

observed_text: ħω_D = kΘ_D is defined by fitting a continuous density of states to 3N modes. It is a spectral edge of a model, not an activation energy.
implied_text: No latched barrier. Θ_D organizes occupation of the last modes; it does not hold a written state.
description: The Debye edge is a cutoff on the oscillator table, not a KV-style memory barrier.
value_text: ħω_D = kΘ_D spectral edge, not a latch
notes: Θ_D is not a melting temperature.

observed_text: Lead has C_p = 26.84 J/(mol K) at 298.15 K (1.08 × 3R) and melts at 600.612 K, 5.7 times its low-temperature Debye temperature. Diamond at room temperature is at 0.25 of 3k per atom.
implied_text: Melting removes the crystalline mode table. Exceeding Θ_D does not.
description: Grid destruction, not Θ_D overrun, ends the 3N crystalline clocks.
value_text: melting ends 3N modes; Θ_D ≠ T_m (Pb T_m = 600.612 K = 5.7 Θ_D)
notes: Cross-cite melting. The earlier remark that diamond does not melt at 1 atm was dropped (not sourced here).

observed_text: Beyond the 3N-th mode there is no lattice mode. In the Debye model that edge is ω_D; in the measured crystals the top branch lies above ν_D (Si 15.5 against 13.3 THz; diamond 39.9 against 38.8 THz).
implied_text: Drive or thermal weight above the top branch finds no lattice mode to occupy. ω_D approximates that edge and is not itself the edge.
description: Above the finite-mode ceiling there is no further phonon channel. The ceiling is the measured top branch; ω_D is a fit.
value_text: ω above top branch (mode absent); ω_D approximate
notes: The heat-capacity approach to 3Nk is a crossover along the Debye function, scale Θ_D.

observed_text: The Debye form assumes a continuous density of states holding 3N modes. A small N gives discrete lines; a single ω_D on a real crystal is a fit that moves with temperature (Pb: 105 K to 87 K).
implied_text: The continuum cutoff is a large-N object. Under-provisioned N is a different spectrum, not a lower Θ_D of the same machine.
description: A cluster does not run a Debye sphere. Continuum Θ_D requires a lattice large enough for the q_D integral.
value_text: N too small → discrete lines, not Debye
notes: No size scale filed.

observed_text: N atoms give exactly 3N normal modes; the count is finite, unlike the modes of the electromagnetic field in a cavity.
implied_text: The clock ceiling exists because the node count is finite. A macroscopic crystal still has a highest mechanical frequency.
description: Finite N is the hardware: 3N modes, no more. The Debye sphere is only a way to place that count on a linear spectrum.
notes: A molecule or cluster has a discrete vibrational set and no continuum Debye sphere.

observed_text: No delay is resolved in the sources read.
implied_text: Collection of p or n is a later step.
description: Prompt nuclear unbinding.
notes: No timing measurement was sourced; the row carries no number.

observed_text: Bd is measured from the capture gamma ray, and the neutron mass is derived from it. QSA does not derive the nuclear force.
implied_text: Bd is a taken input, as me is.
description: Bd taken, not derived.

observed_text: Photoneutrons and photoprotons above threshold: 1.300 mb at 2.62 MeV, 1.474 mb at 2.76 MeV, 2.430 mb at 4.45 MeV, maximum 2.5 mb near 4.4 MeV, 0.5 mb at 22 MeV. Reverse reaction: a 2.223248 MeV capture line, thermal cross-section 334.2 mb.
implied_text: Yield of independent γd conversions.
description: Photodisintegration yield above Bd.

observed_text: Bd = 2 224 566.14(41) eV, from the wavelength of the n–p capture line corrected for recoil. The photodisintegration threshold on a deuteron at rest is 2.225885 MeV (1.32 keV of recoil above Bd).
implied_text: Unbinding gate of a pre-existing pn bound state.
description: 2.224 MeV deuteron unbinding gate.
notes: The neutron mass is derived from Bd, not the reverse (Dewey and Kessler 2000).

observed_text: Below 2.225885 MeV the reaction does not occur. Above it the cross-section rises continuously from zero, as the square root of the excess energy, to a maximum of 2.5 mb near 4.4 MeV.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the collapse. The energy threshold is sharp; the yield above it grows continuously.
description: Eγ below Bd plus recoil closes photodisintegration.

observed_text: One photon and one deuteron; the proton and neutron carry the momentum, so no third body is needed. Yield scales with deuterium column density.
implied_text: N=1 conversion. No metal film, no muon, no recoil partner.
description: Hardware is γ + d.

observed_text: Time lags of 1e-8 s and shorter are recorded in highly overvolted gaps; the formative lag changes between mechanisms near 1e-7 s; the Townsend mechanism alone gives about 1e-5 s. Air at 1 atm holds 2.3 times the field for a 10 ns pulse and a few per cent more for 1 µs. Pulsed oil follows F t^(1/3) A^(1/10) = 0.5. Solids weaken from 1e-8 s (intrinsic) to 1e4 s (erosion).
implied_text: The gate moves with stress duration only where the pulse is shorter than the time the discharge takes to form; in a gas that is below about a microsecond.
description: The field gate moves with stress duration because the discharge takes a finite time to form.
notes: value_si is the formative-lag change between the Townsend and streamer mechanisms. The 10 ns factor is Martin's reading of curves that were not opened.

observed_text: Unlike pair production or a work function, the breakdown field is not a single-node energy. It depends on path, time, defects, heat and the electrode surface. No satisfactory model predicts the intrinsic strength of a solid, and a closed buffer and barrier specification that predicts a polymer's strength from node rules is not in hand.
implied_text: QSA names a field-opened conversion class but cannot attach a first-principles breakdown field. A gas gap has two independent failure routes, multiplication and cathode emission. After the first discharge in a solid the system is a different object.
description: The class is clear; a predictive node-rule Ebd is not. Mapping confidence is medium for that reason.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Contrast with refraction-dielectric (reversible below-threshold polarization of the same insulator).

observed_text: Below the gate: a stable insulating state. Above it: a conducting channel, self-restoring in a gas and permanent in a solid. Gases span a factor of about 400 in strength at equal density; solids run from 17 kV/mm for an alumina to over 600 kV/mm for a 6 µm polyester film.
implied_text: The clean operating envelope is the side of the gate on which nothing has converted.
description: The useful output is continued insulation below the field gate; there is no material-universal breakdown field.
value_text: insulator below the gate; no universal E_bd
notes: value_si is air at 1 cm and 1 atm, kept as a marker only.

observed_text: Air at 1 atm in a uniform field breaks down at 31.6 kV across 1.0 cm (3.16 MV/m); the field is 46 kV/cm at 1 mm and 25.5 kV/cm at 20 cm. Polymer films of 6–125 µm hold 1.5–6e8 V/m. Deposited SiO2 holds 9.0–9.4 MV/cm. Conditioned copper in vacuum breaks down at 159 MV/m macroscopic field, 10.8 GV/m local.
implied_text: The operating gate is a field for a given gap, time and material, not a single quantum hν or I. Behind it stand a voltage floor for the gas mechanism (the Paschen minimum) and a local cathode field for electron emission.
description: Breakdown is a field-opened conversion. The breakdown field is a geometry-, time- and surface-dependent envelope, not a first-principles constant.
value_text: air 3.16 MV/m at 1 cm and 1 atm
notes: Gap, density, humidity (2–3 %), pulse length, area and stress time all move it. The first version put polymer films a decade too low and called the oxide thermal; the opened oxide measurement is for deposited films. Holding the field below the gate costs only the leakage.

observed_text: Tracking leaves a permanent conducting path, usually carbon, on organic insulation; gases are classed as self-restoring. The strength of a solid falls with time of stressing through intrinsic, electromechanical, thermal and erosion mechanisms, and a soft film has no stable thickness below d/d0 = 0.6.
implied_text: A solid that has broken down is a different machine along the track. The original breakdown field is no longer a property of that path.
description: The object after a discharge in a solid is a carbon track or melted channel, not the original insulator with a new number.
notes: Cross-cite ionization-threshold (the microscopic step) and photoconductivity (carriers without necessarily destroying the lattice).

observed_text: Vb = f(pd) for a given gas and cathode, with minima of 327–352 V at 0.55–0.57 torr cm in air and 230–273 V at 1.05–1.15 torr cm in H2. Left of the minimum at low pressure the voltage rises as pd falls. At atmospheric pressure below 5–10 µm it plateaus and then falls about linearly with gap, at 100–350 V/µm, by field emission.
implied_text: pd left of the Paschen minimum raises the voltage needed only while the cathode cannot emit. In a micrometre gap at 1 atm field emission takes over and the gap fails at a lower voltage.
description: Under-provisioning the gas buffer raises the breakdown voltage at low pressure and hands the failure to cathode field emission in a microgap.
value_text: Paschen minimum 327–352 V (air), 230–273 V (H2); microgap 100–350 V/µm
notes: value_si is the lower of two tabulations for air. The first version said very short gaps raise the voltage needed; that is right at low pressure and wrong at atmospheric pressure. The 350 V/µm figure rests on an abstract.

observed_text: Below the breakdown voltage of the gap the insulator passes only leakage. In air no breakdown by multiplication occurs below the Paschen minimum, 327–352 V, at any pd (230–273 V in H2). Gases are self-restoring.
implied_text: Under-threshold voltage is the non-occurrence of the conversion.
description: Below the gate the dielectric continues to support the field; below the Paschen floor a gas gap cannot break down by multiplication.
value_text: E < E_bd (3.16 MV/m for air at 1 cm, 1 atm); V < 327–352 V at any pd
notes: The field value is for a 1 cm gap; it is 46 kV/cm at 1 mm and 44–49 MV/m at the Paschen minimum. The floor depends on the cathode.

observed_text: A single ionization is not breakdown. In a gas the conversion needs αd of 8–10 with cathode feedback (Townsend) or an avalanche of about 1e8 electrons (streamer). The Paschen minimum for air is at pd = 0.55–0.57 torr cm, a gap of 7.2–7.5 µm at 1 atm. Below 5–10 µm at atmospheric pressure the breakdown voltage plateaus and then falls with gap (field emission from the cathode).
implied_text: The gas buffer is a path with enough collisions for multiplication to outrun loss. When it is under-provisioned at low pressure the voltage needed rises; in a micrometre gap at 1 atm, or in vacuum, the cathode surface supplies the electrons and the gap fails at a lower voltage than the gas mechanism requires.
description: Breakdown hardware in a gas is a many-node avalanche path; field emission from the cathode is a second, independent route.
value_text: αd ≈ 8–10; pd_min 0.55–0.57 torr cm in air (7.2–7.5 µm at 1 atm)
notes: The first version said a microgap and a vacuum gap fail to spark because multiplication is under-provisioned; that holds at low pressure only. In a solid or liquid the buffer is the weakest site in the stressed volume or area. The gap at 1 atm is computed here.

observed_text: Elastic response follows the acoustic clock. Plastic flow is rate-dependent: Johnson–Cook factor 1 + C ln(strain rate in s⁻¹) with C from 0.006 (Nickel 200) to 0.060 (Armco iron), which is 1.08 to 1.83 at 10⁶ s⁻¹.
implied_text: The Hookean clock is the acoustic / Debye table. Plastic latency belongs to defect motion, not to the harmonic spring.
description: Microscopic restoration is acoustic-fast; yield latency is a different, slower defect clock.
notes: Extrapolated from fits made up to about 10³ s⁻¹. Cold-spray strain rates are 10⁶–10⁹ s⁻¹.

observed_text: The computed ideal shear strength (5–9 % of the shear modulus) is 12–59 times the shear yield of the metals worked. That gap is the mesoscale dislocation and grain-boundary step, the mechanical counterpart of coercivity against anisotropy field.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer / barrier specification for dislocation nucleation and pinning. The Hookean output does not depend on closing it.
description: Yield / fracture is identified as a mesoscale envelope and is not reduced to a node-level barrier. Same unfinished step as magnet coercivity.
value_text: real yield 12–59× below ideal shear strength; mesoscale
notes: Cross-cite ferromagnetic-hysteresis and permanent-magnet-latch (Hc ≪ Ha). File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: Young's modulus at 20 °C: Al 70.3, Ti 115.7, Cu 129.8, Ni 199.5–219.2, Fe 211.4, mild steel 211.9 GPa. Shear modulus: 26.1, 43.8, 48.3, 76.0–83.9, 81.6, 82.2 GPa. Bulk modulus of diamond 542 GPa.
implied_text: Handbook moduli {E, G, K} are the synchronized small-amplitude restoring output of the coupled nodes, together with a material- and history-dependent yield / fracture envelope.
description: The ion grid emits a GPa-class stiffness set. The same C is the slope v = √(C/ρ).
notes: value_si is mild steel. Speeds computed from K, G and density match measured sound speeds within 0.3 %.

observed_text: Small-strain elasticity is a restoring well, not a latch: stored energy ½ C ε² is returned on unload. Yield is a threshold on that well’s useful range. In crystals the microscopic barrier being crossed is a dislocation Peierls / pinning barrier — measured as a yield stress, not yet specified here as a KV-style node number.
implied_text: The Hookean machine stores and returns ½ C ε². It is not a directional memory. Yield is the well’s useful-range cliff, not a latch write.
description: Elastic energy is returned on unload. Yield is a range threshold, not a remanence barrier.
value_text: ½ C ε² returned; yield ≠ KV

observed_text: The crystal has a finite average shear modulus at its melting point; the liquid has none at acoustic frequencies. The loss of G at T_m is a jump. The liquid keeps a bulk modulus.
implied_text: The solid elastic machine dies with the grid. Compression can remain as a fluid K.
description: Melting removes the static shear modulus discontinuously. K survives.
value_text: G: finite → 0 at T_m (jump); fluid: no static shear
notes: Cross-cite melting and speed-of-sound. The first version read as a continuous softening.

observed_text: Yield constants at room temperature and 1 s⁻¹: OFHC copper 90 MPa, Nickel 200 163, Armco iron 175, 1006 steel 350, 2024-T351 aluminium 265, 4340 steel 792 MPa. Computed ideal shear strength: Al 1.85 GPa, Cu 2.65 GPa, which is 51–59 times the shear yield of OFHC copper and 12–14 times that of 2024 aluminium.
implied_text: Load above yield ends the linear output. Real yield is a mesoscale quantity, 12–59 times below the ideal shear strength in the cases worked.
description: Plastic set or fracture is the load-bearing failure of the Hookean machine. Real metallic yield is far below the ideal bond-breaking estimate.
value_text: yield 90–792 MPa; ideal shear strength 1.85–2.65 GPa
notes: value_si is OFHC copper. Yield is a convention on a continuous curve; it grows as d^(−1/2) with grain refinement and logarithmically with rate. The unsourced E/10 estimate was replaced.

observed_text: A coupled lattice for E and G; a fluid suffices for K. The yield stress is set by a mesoscale population of dislocations and grain boundaries and follows σ_y = σ_0 + k d^(−1/2) with grain size d (coefficients not read).
implied_text: Hookean E is a grid average. Yield is a different, defect-structure buffer on the same crystal.
description: Small-strain stiffness lives on the ion grid; plasticity lives on a mesoscale defect population.
value_text: lattice for E, G; yield ∝ d^(−1/2) (Hall–Petch)
notes: Elastomers are entropy-elastic and not this ion-grid machine.

observed_text: Elastic strain at yield, A/E: OFHC copper 6.9×10⁻⁴, Nickel 200 8.2×10⁻⁴, Armco iron 8.3×10⁻⁴, 1006 steel 1.65×10⁻³, 4340 steel 3.7×10⁻³, 2024 aluminium 3.8×10⁻³.
implied_text: The linear restoring output is specified only inside that small-strain window.
description: The metals tabulated stay linear only to strains of 0.07–0.4 %.
notes: value_si is the largest of the six. Polymers and elastomers are a different, large-strain machine.

observed_text: A spot reaches its temperature in τ = C a²/4λ: 2.2e-7 s for a 10 µm copper spot and 2.2e-9 s at 1 µm. Film breakdown took about 150 µs in a probe measurement; a voltage-driven sintering transition takes less than 2 µs.
implied_text: On any pulse longer than a microsecond the spot temperature follows the instantaneous voltage across the contact.
description: The contact's clock is the thermal diffusion time of the spot, below a microsecond.
notes: The 1 µm value is computed here from the source's constants.

observed_text: No opened source reports contact voltage, breakdown or transition data for a metal-powder paste or slurry carrying current. No saturation voltage per contact has been measured for copper beads or copper powder. A survey finds no single criterion for the transition of a sliding contact.
implied_text: The gates are specified for single static contacts and bead chains. For a moving slurry the voltage per contact, the survival of bridges and the transition condition are open.
description: Nothing is measured for a powder-slurry armature; the mapping stops at static contacts.
value_text: no data for a slurry armature
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. The bead-chain plateau and the powder-bed peak also disagree on what a copper powder does before bridging.

observed_text: After the transition a bead chain has 1–10 Ω against 1e4–1e7 Ω before, set by the largest current applied and unchanged for smaller currents. A copper powder bed is ohmic at less than 1 Ω against about 1e8 Ω.
implied_text: A metallic bridge whose resistance is set by the largest current it has carried, ohmic below that current, and retained at zero power until it is mechanically broken.
description: The stable product is a welded bridge with a resistance fixed by current history.
value_text: R set by the largest current; ohmic below it

observed_text: An insulating film of about 100 Å or more is punctured when the field across it reaches about 1e5–1e6 V/cm (1e7–1e8 V/m); a metallic bridge forms and the contact voltage falls suddenly. That is 0.02–0.2 V for a 2 nm film and 1–10 V for a 100 nm film. Voltages below 30 mV do not permanently damage a film.
implied_text: The film gate is a field at the film's weakest point, separate from the thermal gate of the metal. For a film of a few nanometres the two fall in the same range of voltage.
description: Film puncture (A-fritting) is a field threshold of 1e7–1e8 V/m in the film.
notes: value_si is the lower end. The range rests on two secondary sources; Holm's text was not opened. The film voltages are computed here.

observed_text: Melting voltage across a contact: Cu 0.43 V, Ag 0.37 V, Al 0.3 V, W 1.1 V (Holm's values, read in reproductions). Fe and Ni are disputed: 0.6 and 0.65 V in Holm-derived tables, 0.19 and 0.16 V in Timsit's. The Kohlrausch relation Tm² − T0² = U²/4L gives 0.41 V for copper.
implied_text: The thermal gate is the melting temperature of the spot read as a voltage. Geometry and current do not enter. The spot cannot hold more than this; it grows instead.
description: A contact spot melts at a fixed voltage per metal, a few tenths of a volt.
notes: value_si is copper. Softening is lower (Cu 0.12 V) and is a narrow band of voltage. Holm's book was not opened.

observed_text: Minimum arc voltage and current in a resistive circuit (Holm, read in a reproduction): Cu 13 V and 0.43 A, Ag 12 V and 0.4 A, W 15 V and 1.0–1.1 A; other observers 8–15.2 V and 0.9–1.75 A. The pair is inter-related. In an inductive circuit closure arcs start at open-circuit potentials down to the melting voltage (Cu about 0.4 V, W 1.1 V) on rough surfaces.
implied_text: Above the arc gate the contact becomes a discharge. The tabulated pair is a convention for a resistive circuit; with inductance the floor for a closure arc is the melting voltage.
description: Arc: 12–15 V and 0.4–1.1 A in a resistive circuit; from the melting voltage upward in an inductive one.
notes: value_si is Holm's copper value. Holm's book was not opened.

observed_text: Bridges in the copper bed are about 10–15 µm and the bed is weakly consolidated: a mechanical shock breaks them and returns the bed to its insulating state. A coherer stays conducting until the tube is tapped.
implied_text: The converted state is retained at zero power and erased mechanically. No barrier energy for the erase is measured.
description: Weld bridges are fragile; a shock restores the high-resistance state.
value_text: shock or tapping resets; no measured scale
notes: No source tests a flowing or accelerated powder.

observed_text: A 0.30 mm bed of oxidised copper powder (87.5 µm, 1200 nm Cu2O) holds about 1e8 Ω until the voltage reaches 15.6 ± 2.3 V, then falls by five orders of magnitude to under 1 Ω. The peak field is 52–67 kV/m by bed thickness and falls from 56.6 kV/m unloaded to 17.6 kV/m at 300 MPa. In another copper powder the transition occurs at a fixed dissipated power.
implied_text: A powder bed converts abruptly at a peak field that depends on its state. It shows a peak and a collapse where the bead chain shows a plateau.
description: Copper powder bed: abrupt transition from high to low resistance at tens of kV/m, dependent on compaction.
notes: 4.6–5.8 V per particle layer, computed here by counting one median diameter per layer. One powder and one oxide thickness.

observed_text: An oxidised bead chain under rising current saturates at about 0.4 V per contact for stainless steel, 0.2 V for bronze and 0.3 V for brass, for 1 to 41 beads and any applied force. Copper was not measured. At the plateau the contacts reach about 1050 °C and weld.
implied_text: The contact voltage limits itself at the thermal gate. Below it the contact stays in its high-resistance state; at it the necks grow and the voltage does not rise further.
description: The voltage per contact clamps at 0.2–0.4 V by metal while the bridge forms.
notes: value_si is stainless steel. The temperature is the Kohlrausch relation applied to the measured voltage.

observed_text: A joint conducts through a-spots. The constriction resistance of one spot is ρ/2a: in copper 83 mΩ at 0.1 µm, 8.3 mΩ at 1 µm, 0.83 mΩ at 10 µm. In bead chains the contact radius grows from much less than 0.1 µm to about 10 µm on welding; bridges in a copper powder bed are about 10–15 µm.
implied_text: The buffer is one a-spot. Its radius sets the joint resistance and is a property of load, hardness, film and current history. A chain or bed is that buffer repeated in series.
description: The hardware of a contact is the conducting spot, micrometres across or less; its resistance scales as 1/a.
value_text: a ≪ 0.1 µm before welding; about 10 µm after
notes: value_si is the welded radius. The copper resistances are computed here from ρ = 1.65e-8 Ω m.

observed_text: Specific action g = ∫J² dt; the energy deposited is the integral of resistivity over g. At 1e10 A/m² melting begins after g/J² = 0.81 ms in copper, 0.25 ms in aluminium and 0.13 ms in iron. The scattering time of the carriers in copper at 293 K is 2.46e-14 s.
implied_text: Two clocks. The scattering time is the averaging window of the carriers. The heating clock is the action integral, which runs at J².
description: Joule heating is clocked by the action integral ∫J² dt.
value_text: t = g/J²; Cu 0.81 ms at 10 kA/mm²
notes: One 1975 data set on 0.1 mm wires. Under a pulse the current density of the surface layer enters g, not the total current over the full cross-section (skin-effect).

observed_text: The Lorenz ratio deviates from the Sommerfeld value by up to about 20 % at ordinary temperatures. Matthiessen's rule has measured deviations. The resistivity of a powder body is set by contact films that are described only by a fitted residual resistivity and exponent.
implied_text: The mapping does not reduce the difference between the charge and heat averages, or the contact state of a granular body, to a buffer or clock number.
description: Bulk resistivity closes as an ensemble average; the Lorenz deviations and the powder contact state remain open.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: Resistivity at 293 K in 1e-8 Ω·m: Ag 1.587, Cu 1.678, Al 2.650, W 5.28, Ni 6.93, Fe 9.61. The ratio κ/σT is 2.12–2.90e-8 V²/K² at 273 K against the Sommerfeld value 2.443e-8.
implied_text: An intensive constant ρ(T) independent of sample shape above the mean-free-path scale, a heating rate ρJ² per unit volume, and a ratio to thermal conductivity within about 20 % of L0·T.
description: The averaged carrier population emits one material constant that sets both the voltage drop and the heating.
notes: IACS copper (1.7241e-8 Ω·m) is a convention for commercial metal. Low-carbon steel at 14.3–15.9e-8 Ω·m rests on a design standard and a vendor sheet.

observed_text: Conduction in a bulk metal is a driven dissipative average with a heating rate ρJ² per unit volume. Steps in the resistivity occur at melting, at the oxide film of a powder contact and at a superconducting transition.
implied_text: No barrier holds a state. The gates that appear as steps belong to melting, electrical-contacts and superconductivity.
description: Resistivity has no energy barrier of its own; its steps are borrowed thresholds.
notes: Negative latch spec.

observed_text: Specific action at the start of melting in 0.1 mm wires: Cu 8.05e16, Ag 6.17e16, Al 2.52e16, W 2.43e16, Ni 1.72e16, Fe 1.28e16 A²·s/m⁴. Burst follows at 2.1–2.8 times that and rises with current density. No value was found for any steel.
implied_text: The solid conductor has an action budget. The integral is continuous; the threshold is the phase change it reaches.
description: Joule heating ends the solid conductor at a material-specific action.
notes: One data set (1975); a 2013 study reporting disagreement for Cu and Al was seen only as a snippet. The adiabatic model with IEEE Std 80 constants gives 1.57e16 for steel 1020, 23 % above pure iron wire. Burst is rate-dependent and is not a material constant.

observed_text: At the melting point the resistivity steps up: copper 10.171 → 21.01e-8 Ω·m at 1357.6 K (ratio 2.07), silver 2.06, aluminium 2.34, nickel 1.37, iron 1.055. Exploding-wire data give 1.91 for copper and 1.04 for iron.
implied_text: Loss of lattice order changes the scattering population at a definite temperature. The solid-state constant ends there.
description: Resistivity steps at the melting point; the size of the step is material-specific.
notes: The transition is owned by melting; this row records the resistivity step. Liquid values for Cu and Ni are provisional. The two sources disagree for tungsten (1.08 against 1.29). Do not equate Tm with other thermal thresholds.

observed_text: A powder compact follows ρE = ρres(1 − Θ/ΘM)^(−n), diverging at the tap porosity ΘM; n = 3/2 without oxide and 1.5–3.6 as fitted. Pressed copper compacts measure 1e4–1e5 Ω·m unreduced, about 1e12 times bulk, and 1e-5–1e-6 Ω·m or less after the oxide is reduced at 190–210 °C in forming gas. No value was found for loose or oil-borne copper powder.
implied_text: A granular conductor needs a connected path through contacts whose surface films conduct. Past the percolation bound, or with insulating films, the bulk constant does not apply.
description: A powder body conducts only on the dense side of its percolation bound and only through reduced contacts.
notes: The copper-compact figures were read from a graph; the reduced value is the floor of the plot, at most 60–600 times bulk. Under pressure alone the resistance follows a power law, a crossover. Contact physics is owned by electrical-contacts.

observed_text: ρ = ρ0 + ρi(T), with ρi ∝ T above the Debye temperature and T⁵ well below it. Near 293 K the coefficient is 0.0038–0.0044 per K in Ag, Cu, W and Al and 0.0054–0.0056 per K in Fe and Ni. IACS copper is defined with 0.00393 per °C.
implied_text: The room-temperature constant drifts continuously with the thermal population of the lattice. There is no critical temperature below melting; Fe and Ni change slope at the Curie point without a step.
description: Resistivity rises continuously with temperature, about 0.4 % per kelvin in copper.
notes: Coefficients are slopes between the 273 K and 300 K table rows. The 0.00160 per °C listed for steel 1020 in IEEE Std 80 is a constant of that standard's fusing formula, not a measured slope. Bloch–Grüneisen is derived for a special model.

observed_text: Mean free path in copper at room temperature is 39–40 nm. A film of thickness d has ρ = ρ0[1 + (3/8)(Λ0/d)(1 − p)] in the thick-film form; grain boundaries add to it, and measured copper films rise faster than the surface term with p = 0 predicts.
implied_text: The bulk constant is an average over many scattering events. It holds when every dimension of the conductor and of its grains is large against the mean free path; below that it rises continuously.
description: Resistivity needs a statistical buffer: dimensions large against the mean free path.
notes: The surface term adds 37.5 % at d = Λ0 with p = 0, at the edge of the thick-film form. Fuchs (1938), Sondheimer (1952) and Mayadas and Shatzkes (1970) were not opened. The size dependence is a crossover with no minimum size.

observed_text: Electron–lattice energy transfer in thin copper films takes 1–4 ps, increasing with laser fluence.
implied_text: The relevant energy scale is kT against E_F, or against a gap Δ when one is present.
description: Calorimetry reads an already-finished electronic average.
notes: One metal measured. Heat deposited faster than this is held first by about 1 % of the heat capacity.

observed_text: γ is taken from measurement. The free-electron estimate is right for Ag and low by a factor of 1.4–1.5 for Cu and Al; in Pd the measured value is 1.7 times the band value.
implied_text: QSA takes the measured γ (or D(E_F), or T_F) as the material specification.
description: γ is located as a material coefficient and is not derived from node count.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. k is defined.

observed_text: C = γT + βT³ at low temperature. γ in mJ/mol K²: Cu 0.690–0.696, Ag 0.645–0.652, Al 1.35, Fe 4.89–4.90, Ni 7.04, Pd 9.42–9.45; CeAl3 1620. Free-electron values: Cu 0.505, Ag 0.645, Al 0.912.
implied_text: A heat capacity linear in T, with a material coefficient γ, is the averaged energy uptake of the Fermi-surface slice.
description: The stable output is C_e = γT. γ is taken from measurement, not derived here.
value_text: C_e = γT; γ = 0.65 (Ag) to 9.4 (Pd) mJ/mol K²; CeAl3 1620
notes: Ni rests on a compiled handbook page. Measured over free-electron: 1.38 (Cu), 1.00 (Ag), 1.48 (Al).

observed_text: The operating condition is no gap at the Fermi energy. In aluminium below Tc = 1.163 K the linear term is replaced by a roughly exponential one.
implied_text: The operating condition is an ungapped Fermi surface. The gaps that kill γT are owned by other families; they appear here only as the threshold that removes the average.
description: γT requires an open Fermi surface, not a latching barrier.
notes: Cross-cite superconductivity and semiconductor-gap-absorption.

observed_text: A material with a gap at the Fermi energy has no metallic γT. No number is filed.
implied_text: Without a contributing slice at E_F there is no electronic linear term at any N or T.
description: No Fermi surface, no γT. That is a missing population, not a cooled metal.
notes: A property of the material class; no opened source was used. Cross-cite semiconductor-gap-absorption.

observed_text: In aluminium (Tc = 1.163 K) the superconducting electronic heat capacity for 0.25 < T/Tc < 0.5 follows C_es/γTc = 7.1 exp(−1.34 Tc/T), 13 % of the normal value at Tc/4; below that it lies above the exponential, by a factor of 4 at the lowest temperature. The heat capacity jumps at Tc.
implied_text: The contributing Fermi-surface slice has been removed, not merely cooled. This entry owns that the gap kills γT, not the gap itself.
description: A superconducting gap replaces the linear electronic heat capacity with an exponentially small remnant.
value_text: T < Tc: γT replaced by ∼exp(−1.34 Tc/T) (Al)
notes: A phase transition at Tc. Cross-cite superconductivity.

observed_text: γT falls linearly to zero in the normal state; aluminium follows C = γT + βT³ from 4.0 K down to 0.11 K. Above 3.8 K (Cu) or 7.4 K (Al) the lattice term is the larger; at 300 K the electronic share is 0.85 % (Cu), 1.7 % (Al), and about 6 % and 8 % (Fe, Ni, extrapolated).
implied_text: The average is still defined; the output is no longer a usable reading. The slice has shrunk, not gapped.
description: Cooling a normal metal sends γT into the calorimeter noise without a gap-closure event.
value_text: γT ∝ T; equal to lattice term at 3.8 K (Cu), 7.4 K (Al)
notes: Linear, with no critical value. The Fe and Ni shares assume the low-temperature γ holds to 300 K.

observed_text: Free-electron Fermi temperatures: Cu 8.16e4 K, Ag 6.38e4 K, Al 13.6e4 K. The participating fraction T/T_F is 0.37 % for Cu at 300 K. There is no count at which electronic heat capacity begins.
implied_text: The hardware is the T-dependent Fermi-surface population of order (T/T_F)N, not a fixed node count. A metal with no Fermi surface has no such population at any N.
description: Electronic heat capacity uses a shrinking statistical slice, not a single buffer size.
value_text: ∼(T/T_F)N; T_F = 6.4e4–13.6e4 K (Ag, Cu, Al, free-electron model)
notes: Fermi temperatures are free-electron model values, not measurements.

observed_text: Setting needs a cool through the ordering temperature in a field or from a remanent state; zero-field cooling from a demagnetized state gives no shift. The blocking temperature rises with measurement sweep rate.
implied_text: The pin is set by a thermal write and is itself thermally activated: its blocking temperature depends on the observation clock.
description: Pin-setting latency is a laboratory field-cool; reading the pin depends on the sweep rate.
notes: Training (the shift falls roughly as 1/√n over consecutive loops) is a relaxation of the pin.

observed_text: The ideal-interface estimate exceeds the measured coupling by a factor of three to several orders of magnitude; roughness, uncompensated spins, and antiferromagnetic domains are the named ingredients. TB often lies well below bulk TN.
implied_text: QSA does not reduce the interface to a buffer/barrier number, and does not give a portable KV line for TB/TN.
description: Hex and TB/TN remain interface- and grain-level data without a closed specification.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason. Loop shifts also occur with pins that are not antiferromagnets.

observed_text: The hysteresis loop is shifted along the field axis rather than centered at H = 0, generally opposite to the cooling field. In Fe/FeF2 a large cooling field (70 kOe against 2 kOe) reverses the sign.
implied_text: Stable output is an offset −Hex of the FM loop and a remanent FM state whose zero-field point is no longer symmetric.
description: The machine emits a unidirectional loop offset, not a centered remanence.
notes: An increase of FM coercivity often accompanies the shift; the two numbers are not the same artifact.

observed_text: Holding the shifted remanent point costs zero continuous power. Energy is spent to field-cool (set the pin) and to traverse the shifted loop (write the FM).
implied_text: The offset remanent state is a latch: set once, held at zero watts below TB.
description: Holding the shifted remanence costs zero watts.

observed_text: The loop is centered at −Hex. Co–CoO particles: 1600 Oe at 77 K, up to 9500 Oe at 4–10 K. Interface energy 0.004–0.47 erg/cm² for common pins, up to 3.5 for oxidized Co. A 4 nm Co core that blocks near 6–10 K alone stays blocked to 220–290 K when pinned.
implied_text: The antiferromagnet adds a unidirectional barrier. In a small grain it can be the dominant barrier, not only an offset on an existing latch.
description: Exchange bias is a second, unidirectional barrier that can stabilize the ferromagnet as well as offset its loop.
notes: The ideal-interface (Meiklejohn–Bean) estimate is too large by a factor of 3 to several orders.

observed_text: The shift falls to zero at TB. FeMn 380–480 K (TN 490 K), IrMn 400–520 K (690 K), NiO 450–500 K (520 K), Co/CoO(25 Å) 180 K (291 K). A film has a distribution of blocking temperatures, and TB rises with sweep rate.
implied_text: Thermal unblocking of the pin removes the shift and leaves a centered loop, with coercivity still enhanced up to TN. The ferromagnet stays ordered.
description: The pin unblocks at TB, a rate-dependent crossover that is not the Néel transition.
value_text: T > TB (≤ TN of the layer)
notes: TB ≤ TN holds against the layer's own ordering temperature; annealed polycrystalline FeMn is listed at 420–570 K against a bulk 490 K.

observed_text: The shift falls as 1/tFM. Below a critical antiferromagnet thickness of a few nanometres it drops abruptly to zero; the critical thickness is an order of magnitude smaller for the more anisotropic fluoride.
implied_text: FM-side buffer dilution and AFM-side under-provisioning are the two spatial failures of the nested latch.
description: Too thick an FM film dilutes Hex; too thin an AFM film unblocks the pin.
value_text: H_ex ~ 1/t_FM; AFM too thin → no pin
notes: Ferromagnet dilution is the crossover on this row. The antiferromagnet-thickness limit is a threshold. Damage to the interface is a third failure with no measured scale filed.

observed_text: The shift is roughly proportional to 1/tFM up to several hundred nm. It is independent of antiferromagnet thickness above about 20 nm and zero at a few nm (6 nm in one IrMn study). The coupling reaches through Ag, Au or Cu spacers up to 50 Å.
implied_text: Hardware is an antiferromagnet thick and anisotropic enough to hold its direction, a ferromagnet thin enough not to dilute the interface term, and proximity within a few nanometres.
description: Two ordered bodies plus a coupling with a reach of nanometres; missing any of the three removes the shift.
value_text: AFM ≳ a few nm; FM thin; separation ≲ 5 nm
notes: The first version said a separated AFM and FM show no shift, with no length.

observed_text: V is quoted at 632–633 nm and 1064 nm. Cold-plasma Faraday rotation (ω≫ωc, ωp) goes as 1/ω², i.e. λ²; it is measured at about 100–200 MHz, 11–200 times the ionospheric plasma frequency of 1–9 MHz.
implied_text: The carrier is optical or radio. In a plasma the carrier must be above the plasma frequency for the wave to propagate; above it the rotation fades as 1/ω² and does not stop at the edge.
description: Clock is the carrier; the load-bearing resource is the VBL product, not a cycle time.
value_text: optical / radio carrier; plasma rotation ∝ λ² above ωp
notes: Cross-cite cyclotron-resonance: resonant absorption at ω=ωc. Do not file the two as one artifact.

observed_text: The mapping takes V as measured and does not derive TGG's value. The 0.81 RM prefactor follows from e, m_e, c and ε0 in the cold-plasma model.
implied_text: The magneto-optical coupling is located as a measured path coefficient, not derived.
description: V is taken. Combined with crossover-only failure modes, that keeps the mapping Medium.
notes: Paramagnetic V(T) touches curie-paramagnetism; the Faraday output is a path integral, not a susceptibility reading.

observed_text: TGG: −131 to −134 rad T^{-1} m^{-1} at 632 nm, −38 at 1064 nm. Fused silica: 3.7 rad T^{-1} m^{-1} at 633 nm. A double pass doubles the rotation.
implied_text: A rotation angle linear in B and L, non-reciprocal, with a material- and frequency-specific V (or an RM in the plasma case).
description: The synchronized magneto-optical population emits θ=VBL, not a latched moment.
notes: Per-tesla Verdet; value_si left null. Plasma form ψ = ψ0 + RM λ² with RM = 0.81∫ n_e B_∥ dl, measured at 100–200 MHz, far above the plasma frequency. TGG values are from tertiary pages, silica from a secondary citation.

observed_text: θ = VBL in the linear regime. θ∝B through zero. Non-reciprocity: two passes through the same B double θ.
implied_text: No latch. B is a load-bearing resource, not a gate with a finite onset. Tag field-threshold marks that resource, not a step-function threshold.
description: Faraday has a field resource, not an energy barrier that stores a written polarization.
value_text: θ ∝ B through zero; no latch
notes: Tesla-scale B is the laboratory class, not an onset.

observed_text: With B→0 the rotation is gone.
implied_text: Field under-provisioning sends θ→0 linearly. There is no finite onset field.
description: B→0 is a linear fade, θ ∝ B.

observed_text: θ = VBL is linear in L. The rotation falls below a given polarimetric floor when the product VBL does. Absorption limits the usable L.
implied_text: Path below the VBL detection budget → no measurable rotation. A slightly short path is a smaller angle, not a disappeared machine.
description: Spatial failure is a detection budget, linear in L.
notes: Product of V, B and L; no minimum length, so value_si is null. Opacity is a second path failure with no filed scale.

observed_text: TGG's V falls from −131 to −38 rad T^{-1} m^{-1} between 632 and 1064 nm and rises toward cryogenic temperatures. In a plasma the rotation goes as λ²: a factor of 4 less per doubling of frequency.
implied_text: The coupling per unit path falls continuously with wavelength (dielectric), frequency (plasma) or rising temperature (paramagnetic medium).
description: A zero-V medium is a Faraday path with no accumulator.
value_text: V falls with λ (TGG), with T (paramagnet); plasma rotation ∝ λ²
notes: Cross-cite curie-paramagnetism for the moment ensemble behind paramagnetic V(T); no functional form filed.
