observed_text: Path for a 45° rotation at 1 T: 6.0 mm of TGG at 632 nm, 2.1 cm of TGG at 1064 nm, 21 cm of fused silica at 633 nm. The interstellar case uses parsecs of dilute plasma. The rotation is proportional to L and has no minimum length.
implied_text: The buffer is the path L through a magneto-optically active population (bound charges with a magnetic splitting, or a magnetized plasma), not a film thickness.
description: Faraday hardware is a path budget.
notes: value_si is the TGG path for 45° at 1 T and 1064 nm, not a minimum. Silica needs about 21 cm; interstellar RM uses parsecs.

observed_text: Reversal is nucleation, forward growth, then slower sideways growth. A written domain grows logarithmically with pulse length beyond 20 µs. In 5–30 nm BaTiO3 capacitors a multidomain state re-forms within 10–500 µs.
implied_text: A static pattern has no ongoing clock cost. Write latency of a domain pattern is wall motion, not the phonon period.
description: Polar walls inherit the THz ionic clock; the partition itself moves on a much slower pinning-limited clock.
value_text: nucleation and wall growth; logarithmic in time; 10–500 µs relaxation
notes: The optical-phonon clock and the optical write channel of the first version had no opened source and were removed.

observed_text: Which wall types and what period a sample shows is an electrostatic, elastic and pinning problem whose output is imaged. Continuum wall coefficients are rough estimates. Wall pinning as the origin of Ec is open.
implied_text: QSA does not produce g and α from a more primitive buffer, and does not select the imaged pattern from node rules. The same mesoscale Ec gap reappears as pinning. Charged-wall screening is an extra constraint.
description: Pattern choice and the pinning that sets technical Ec remain mesoscale data; the wall-width and no-pattern cliffs do not depend on closing them.
value_text: pattern taken; pinning and Ec underived
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason. Does not close polar-depolarization-buffer.

observed_text: Net polarization ranges from zero (stripe domains in an unscreened film) to the spontaneous value (one domain). Walls are imaged by electron microscopy, holography and x-ray scattering and are static at rest.
implied_text: Stable output is a static partition of the polar population, with measured nm-class wall width and a net P set by how closed the pattern is.
description: Domains emit a held partition, not a requirement of a large net dipole.
notes: Imaging methods are those of the opened sources.

observed_text: Holding a static domain pattern costs zero continuous power: it is a static configuration. Moving walls around a loop dissipates the loop area.
implied_text: Hold-power of a static partition is zero. Wall motion around a P–E loop dissipates the loop area owned by remanence.
description: Holding a polar domain pattern costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when walls move.

observed_text: Calculated wall energies: BaTiO3 180° 7.2–7.5 mJ/m² (0 K) and 16 mJ/m² (finite temperature); PbTiO3 132 mJ/m² (180°) and 35 mJ/m² (90°). An experimental estimate for the PbTiO3 90° wall is 50 mJ/m². Holding a static partition costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Each domain is the parent polar well. Partition cost is wall area times wall energy per area. Pinning is the mesoscale Ec gap.
description: Partition cost is wall energy per area; static patterns have no hold-power bill.
notes: All calculated except the 50 mJ/m² estimate. 90° walls are cheaper than 180° walls in PbTiO3.

observed_text: Under a field, reversal is nucleation and growth with an activation field or a broad distribution of waiting times; wall velocity varies continuously with field. No opened source gives a field at which the last wall is removed.
implied_text: Applied E expels walls → the partition is gone. The local well is still present; remanent P after that step is the parent latch.
description: Poling is destruction of the domain pattern, not of the local polar well.
notes: The Curie point removes the polar phase and the domains with it (threshold); that is filed on remanence.

observed_text: No single-domain size was found. PbTiO3 films without free charge form 180° stripe domains from 420 Å down to 12 Å; BaTiO3 nanocubes hold a monodomain state and switch at about 5 nm. Which occurs depends on compensation of the bound surface charge.
implied_text: One domain or many is set by the electrical boundary (screening), not by a particle size.
description: Single-domain condition is a crossover in screening; there is no critical size.
value_text: no critical size; stripes to 1.2 nm, monodomain at 5 nm
notes: The 10 nm to tens-of-nm BaTiO3 class of the first version was not supported. Does not close polar-depolarization-buffer.

observed_text: A 180° wall lies parallel to P because a wall with net bound charge is unfavourable. Charged walls exist when compensated: in BaTiO3 they conduct at 10^9 times the bulk conductivity through an electron gas. Bound charge would be 2Ps = 0.53 C/m² (head-to-head 180°) or 0.37 C/m² (90°).
implied_text: Charged walls are an extra electrostatic buffer the magnetic analog does not carry. Uncompensated bound charge is the same family as slab depolarization.
description: A polar partition must provision screening at charged walls; a neutral 180° wall does not.
notes: The bound-charge figures are computed from Ps = 0.263 C/m².

observed_text: A 90° wall separates domains whose polar axes are at right angles. Measured widths are 1–5 nm in crystals and 14 nm in ceramics. In PbTiO3 its calculated energy (35 mJ/m²) is 3.8 times lower than that of the 180° wall, with a very small barrier to motion.
implied_text: 90° walls are the strain face of the polar partition. They support oscillator-grid / piezo as well as polar-latch.
description: A 90° wall emits a strain reconfiguration locked to the partition, not polarity reversal alone.
notes: The first version said 90° walls cost more; the calculated energies are the other way round.

observed_text: 180° wall: about one lattice constant (BaTiO3) and one to two lattice constants (PbTiO3) by first-principles calculation, 0.4–0.8 nm. 90° wall measured: 1.0–2.1 nm in PbTiO3, 2–5 and 4–6 nm in BaTiO3, 14 nm in ceramics.
implied_text: The wall is a measured spatial buffer, not a mathematical point. Narrower than that and the two domains have merged.
description: A resolved polar domain wall is a nanometre-class strip: ~0.5 nm for 180° BaTiO3, a few nm for 90°, 1–10 nm as a class.
value_text: 0.4–0.8 nm calculated (180°); 1–5 nm measured (90°, crystals); 14 nm (ceramics)
notes: value_si is the nanometre order. The 180° width is a calculation. Measured hard-magnet walls (4–9 nm in Nd2Fe14B) lie inside the polar range.

observed_text: Switching is nucleation at the electrode, forward growth, then slower sideways growth of domains. Without full compensation the net polarization of a 5–30 nm BaTiO3 capacitor relaxes between 10 and 500 µs.
implied_text: The write clock is nucleation and domain growth under the applied field; an unscreened state has its own relaxation clock of tens to hundreds of microseconds.
description: Switching clock is nucleation and wall growth; relaxation of an under-screened film is 10–500 µs.
notes: The first version named an optical-phonon / THz clock; no source for a frequency was opened and the phrase was removed. Key name kept for stable joins.

observed_text: Ec is taken from loops and from the empirical d^(-2/3) law. The depolarizing field is measured in one capacitor system and agrees there with electrostatics. A general screening requirement for a given retention time is not filed, and no polar KV criterion exists.
implied_text: QSA does not derive Ec from the Landau well, nor a laboratory-stability volume from node rules.
description: Write threshold and grain/depolarization buffer remain mesoscale data without a closed QSA specification.
value_text: Ec empirical; screening requirement not specified
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason.

observed_text: Spontaneous polarization of BaTiO3 at room temperature is 0.263 C/m² (0.15 in older flux-grown crystals). LiNbO3 71 µC/cm², LiTaO3 60 µC/cm². Remanent polarization of a PZT film is about 40 µC/cm².
implied_text: Stable output is remanent polarization and the associated bound charge / field at E = 0.
description: The polar latch emits a material-typical remanent P, not a linear dielectric that returns to P = 0.
value_text: Ps = 0.263 C/m² (BaTiO3); Pr about 0.4 C/m² (PZT film)
notes: value_si is the BaTiO3 spontaneous polarization. No bulk-ceramic Pr table was opened.

observed_text: The sample stays poled at zero applied field and zero continuous power: a static configuration. An under-screened film is the exception and relaxes on its own.
implied_text: Stable remanent polarization and bound charge / field at zero continuous power, inside the Tc / grain / electrode / lattice envelope.
description: Holding remanent polarity costs zero watts. Energy is the P–E loop area only.

observed_text: A polar double well holds ±Pr at E = 0 at zero continuous power. Energy per cycle is the loop area. Bulk coercive fields are typically several kV/cm; 300–400 kV/cm in 5–30 nm BaTiO3 films; Ec scales as d^(-2/3) from 100 µm to 200 nm.
implied_text: The latch is the polar well. Energy is spent only on transitions. The write threshold is Ec, not the Landau barrier of a perfect crystal.
description: Remanent polarity is protected by a lattice-locked double well at zero hold-power; write cost is the P–E loop area.
value_text: double well below Tc; Ec several kV/cm (bulk) to 300–400 kV/cm (5–30 nm films)
notes: Ec is a loop intercept set by nucleation and growth, with an empirical thickness law; it is not derived from the Landau well.

observed_text: BaTiO3 Curie point 120 °C (393 K; 120–130 °C quoted). PbTiO3 760 K. PZT grades 195–365 °C. LiNbO3 1413–1475 K; LiTaO3 874–958 K. Above it the polar phase is gone.
implied_text: kT closing the polar well destroys the latch. Further BaTiO3 polar-phase changes (~5 °C, −90 °C) are structure changes of an already-latched state.
description: Thermal collapse of the polar latch at the ferroelectric Curie point.
notes: value_si is BaTiO3. PbTiO3 rests on one tertiary source. A phase transition.

observed_text: Polarization of PbTiO3 films falls gradually below about 200 Å and is reduced but present at 24 Å. Net remanence is lost first: by relaxation when the residual depolarizing field reaches Ec (5–30 nm BaTiO3 capacitors), or by 180° stripe domains in films without free charge (12–420 Å). The calculated critical thickness is about 6 unit cells (BaTiO3 with SrRuO3) and 2–7 unit cells (PbTiO3).
implied_text: Under-screened bound charge empties the net polarization of the latch while the polar phase remains. The loss is continuous in thickness and depends on the electrode.
description: Depolarization loss of net remanence in thin films: a crossover set by screening, with a model threshold at a few unit cells.
value_text: continuous below ~20 nm; model threshold 2–7 unit cells
notes: Key name kept for stable joins; no superparaelectric (thermal-volume) criterion was found. The critical thickness is a zero-temperature calculation.

observed_text: The polar phase is stable down to 3 unit cells (1.2 nm) in PbTiO3 films and switching is seen in crystals of about 5 nm. Net remanence needs compensation of the bound surface charge: in 5–30 nm BaTiO3 capacitors with SrRuO3 electrodes the residual depolarizing field is comparable to the coercive field (300–400 kV/cm).
implied_text: Hardware is a polar lattice plus a source of compensating charge. The buffer is the screening (fraction of bound charge left uncompensated), not a single length or a thermal volume.
description: The polar phase needs about a nanometre; a net remanent polarization needs screening complete to about one part in a thousand.
value_text: polar phase to 1.2 nm; remanence set by screening
notes: No thermal-volume (KV) criterion was found for a ferroelectric. The 6-unit-cell critical thickness is a calculation for one electrode.

observed_text: Precession scale γ/2π = 28.025 GHz/T (CODATA 2022). Reversal is thermally activated, so the switching field of a single-domain particle depends on waiting time and temperature. In simulated loops over five decades of sweep rate the coercivity depends on the sweep rate.
implied_text: The latch has a 28 GHz/T precession carrier. The loop itself depends on the clock: a coercivity quoted without a sweep rate and a temperature is a convention.
description: Holding remanence does not run the 28 GHz/T carrier as a power draw; the write field depends on how long and how fast the field is applied.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency. The first version named eddy currents as a limit on loop traversal; no opened source supports that and it was dropped.

observed_text: Commercial sintered Nd-Fe-B reaches about 0.2 Ha (1.2 T against 7.5 T, about 15 %); 20–30 % of Ha is the general figure for permanent magnets, and one text puts the overestimate at one order of magnitude. Coherent rotation predicts Hc = 2K1/μ0Ms for an aligned particle. One review reports both a nucleation and a grain-boundary-pinning reading of sintered Nd-Fe-B.
implied_text: QSA has no buffer/barrier specification that produces Hc from nucleation, grain boundaries, local demagnetizing fields and wall pinning. The literature's own form, αHa − Neff·Ms, carries two fitted numbers.
description: Measured Hc is a mesoscale, clock-dependent write field at 15–30 % of Ha. The Curie threshold and the zero-hold-power clause do not depend on closing it.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. The 1.2 T figure is one grade (N50), not a class range.

observed_text: The first sintered Nd-Fe-B magnet has a remanence of 1.23 T. The energy lost per unit volume in one complete cycle is the area of the loop, W = ∮H dB = ∮H dJ.
implied_text: Stable output is remanence at H = 0 plus a dissipation equal to the loop area each time the major loop is cycled.
description: The loop is the latch cycle: a remanent state at zero field, and dissipation only when the state is cycled.
value_text: Mr at H = 0; W = ∮H dB per major-loop cycle
notes: The loop area is the cost of the major-loop write and is not a floor: a single-domain Permalloy bit has been operated at 1.45 kBT.

observed_text: Holding a remanent point costs zero continuous power: it is a static configuration, and no source reports a dissipation at rest.
implied_text: Zero hold power plus a protocol-dependent write cost is the latch accounting.
description: Holding either remanent branch costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when the state is written.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B K1 is 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³ from fits to magnetization curves; the anisotropy field 2K1/μ0Ms is 6.7–7.7 T. The energy lost per unit volume in one complete cycle is the loop area ∮H dB. A single-bit operation in Permalloy nanomagnets dissipated 1.45 ± 0.35 kBT. Holding a remanent point costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: The barrier that protects remanence is the anisotropy barrier of the permanent-magnet latch. Hold cost is zero. The loop area is the cost of a major-loop write; the measured floor for one bit is of order kBT.
description: Hysteresis is the write/erase cycle of the anisotropy latch: zero hold-power, a major-loop cost equal to the loop area, and a per-bit floor near the Landauer bound.
value_text: K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³; W = ∮H dB per major loop
notes: value_si is the lower edge of the K1 range. K1 = 4.5 MJ/m³ and μ0Ha = 7–8 T of the first version were not found in any opened source. The write field is Hc, about 15–20 % of Ha in sintered Nd-Fe-B; that mesoscale step is the §4.6 gap.

observed_text: Curie temperature, where the spontaneous magnetization vanishes: iron 770 °C (1043 K) or 1044 K; Nd2Fe14B 585 K in the discovery paper, 585–593 K across three reviews, with 565 K and 558 K in two other opened papers.
implied_text: Thermal destruction of the ordered moment removes the loop. This is a phase transition, distinct from the soft limit and from the volume crossover.
description: No ordered moment above Tc, so no remanent branch and no hysteresis loop.
value_text: T > Tc (585 K Nd2Fe14B, sources 585–593 K; 1043–1044 K Fe)
notes: value_si is the discovery-paper value for Nd2Fe14B. The grain-volume limit is a crossover, filed as superparamagnetism.

observed_text: Coercivity runs from 0.3–2 A/m (permalloy) through 10–100 A/m (polycrystalline iron) and 136 kA/m (one alnico) to 960 kA/m (first sintered Nd-Fe-B), 5.7 to 6.5 decades. The soft/hard boundary at 1000 A/m, or at about 40 A/m, is a convention.
implied_text: Remanence in an open body is lost when the coercivity is below the body's demagnetizing field. The fall-off along the coercivity scale is continuous, and the metal stays ferromagnetic.
description: The soft limit is a crossover along a six-decade coercivity continuum: loss of a usable write barrier with ferromagnetic order intact.
value_text: Hc from 0.3 A/m to ~10^6 A/m; soft/hard cut at 10^3 A/m by convention
notes: value_si is the conventional class boundary; no measured threshold exists. The first version gave 10^2–10^3 A/m as the typical soft coercivity; typical values are 0.3–100 A/m. Retention in any shape needs Hc > Ms/2.

observed_text: A magnet that keeps its remanence in any shape needs a coercivity above half its magnetization: Hc/Ms is 0.75 for the first sintered Nd-Fe-B magnet and below 1e-4 for polycrystalline iron. Single particles of 15–30 nm reverse by thermal activation over one barrier, with an activation volume close to the particle volume. The 25 kBT stability cut is a convention for a 100 s measurement.
implied_text: Minimum hardware is an ordered volume with an anisotropy barrier, down to one single-domain particle. A bulk loop is the sum over a population of grains and walls, each reversing at its own field.
description: The loop needs a latched grain whose barrier outlasts the measurement and whose coercivity exceeds the body's demagnetizing field.
value_text: grain above the thermal cut; Hc above the demagnetizing field; no single loop N
notes: Grain sizes are owned by superparamagnetism. The soft/hard split follows the coercivity and is independent of Tc: iron is ordered up to 1043 K with Hc/Ms below 1e-4.

observed_text: There is no voltage-frequency lock on a fully superconducting loop at rest (V=0 around the path). A SQUID reads the same integer against the Josephson clock of the interrupting junctions.
implied_text: The relevant latency is the screening response of the parent condensate (London / plasma scales on meissner), not a Josephson oscillation of the loop itself.
description: A quiet superconducting loop holds n at V=0; it does not run the 483.6 MHz/μV clock until a weak link is inserted.
notes: Cross-cite josephson-effect for the SQUID readout clock.

observed_text: The single-valuedness relation uses q=2e as the measured charge increment. Φ0 = h/2e is a defined SI combination taken from that increment.
implied_text: The 2e in h/2e is taken from the measured quantum, not derived from node rules. No pairing story is added to close it.
description: Same open charge increment as on josephson-effect; the integer condition itself is not in doubt.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. λ and ξ that set how small a hole or vortex core can be are owned by meissner and type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: The flux through a superconducting ring is quantized in units of Φ0 = h/2e = 2.067 833 848…×10⁻¹⁵ Wb (exact since 2019).
implied_text: A trapped fluxoid equal to nΦ0, held at zero continuous power for as long as the loop, the gap, and the phase-slip barrier remain inside the envelope.
description: The machine's stable product is the integer fluxoid n h/2e.
notes: Combined with the AC Josephson lock this is the same constant in a different geometry. Chargeless analog is h/m4 on superfluid-helium-4.

observed_text: The stored integer changes by a phase slip: the order parameter goes to zero at one point of the path and the phase jumps by 2πn, with a voltage pulse. Quantum phase slips are measurable in wires below about 50 nm and dominate near 10 nm.
implied_text: Changing the stored integer by one requires a phase slip: a local collapse of the gap on the loop, or a vortex crossing the wall. That barrier keeps n fixed and vanishes if any section is driven normal, or if T → Tc.
description: The stored integer is a latch: a phase-slip barrier protects n at zero continuous power.
notes: Contrast with bose-einstein-condensate, which is not held at zero continuous power.

observed_text: Warming the loop through Tc releases the constraint and the integer condition disappears.
implied_text: Thermal collapse of the parent condensate erases the fluxoid latch.
description: The trapped integer dies with the superconducting path at Tc.
notes: Material Tc values live on superconductivity. A weak spot or a current near the loop Ic lets n step without shifting Φ0.

observed_text: Opening the ring, driving a section normal, or a lead / normal gap on the circumference releases the constraint and the integer condition disappears.
implied_text: Topology failure: if the path is not closed, the fluxoid is not conserved and there is no trapped integer.
description: A broken loop cannot hold nΦ0.
notes: Electrode-scale H > Hc or Hc2 destroys the path itself.

observed_text: The loop must be a closed superconducting path. A break, a normal section, or T > Tc anywhere on the circumference removes quantization of the trapped flux.
implied_text: A closed superconducting path is the hardware. The hole (or vortex core) is the region the condensate does not fill; the load-bearing buffer is the surrounding closed path.
description: Flux quantization requires a closed condensate path; an open ring is not this machine.
notes: The path must sit inside the superconductivity envelope. A vortex as the hole is owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: In a thick ring (wall thickness large compared with the London depth λ) the trapped flux itself is nΦ0. In a thin-walled cylinder the conserved quantity is the fluxoid; Little–Parks still has period Φ0.
implied_text: For the trapped flux (not merely the fluxoid) to sit at nΦ0, the wall must be thick enough that screening currents live in a surface layer of depth λ and the interior supercurrent vanishes.
description: Wall thickness versus λ selects flux integers versus fluxoid integers; both are the same constraint in two buffer regimes.
notes: A wall thinner than λ still fixes the fluxoid. λ values are on meissner. The Little–Parks period is cited to a letter that was not opened.

observed_text: D of hydrogen at 298 K from the opened Arrhenius fits: Ni 5.1e-14, Pd 7.7e-11, Fe 7.3e-9 m²/s. Crossing 1 µm takes 20 s, 13 ms and 0.14 ms; 100 µm takes 55 h, 130 s and 1.4 s. In 100 µs hydrogen moves 2.3 nm in Ni, 88 nm in Pd and 850 nm in Fe.
implied_text: The clock is the interstitial hop read as D(T). A drive shorter than x²/D does not move hydrogen a distance x.
description: Room-temperature hydrogen transport over a micrometre takes seconds in nickel and milliseconds or less in palladium and iron.
value_text: x²/D for 1 µm: Ni 20 s; Pd 13 ms; Fe 0.14 ms
notes: The Fe fit is taken from a secondary; the Pd fit from an abstract. value_si is the nickel 1 µm time.

observed_text: The opened sources give no barrier that scales with the volume of a trapped hydrogen cluster, no size series of hydrogen retention in nickel, and no measured trap energy for nickel.
implied_text: A volume-proportional barrier is sourced only for the coherent hydride transition. Whether any trapped population has one is open.
description: No measured volume-scaling barrier exists for trapped hydrogen; the nickel trap data are thin.
notes: Three behaviours share this entry: an ensemble average (solubility), a hysteretic transition (hydride) and a per-atom trap.

observed_text: Hydride formation expands the lattice: β-PdH0.58 is 3.5–3.7 % larger in lattice parameter than Pd (10.9 % in volume); NiH is 5.9 % larger than Ni (18.7 %). Polycrystalline nickel magnetostriction is −33 to −35 ppm and its thermal expansion is 13.4e-6 per K.
implied_text: The stable output of a hydride former is an occupancy with a percent-level strain. That strain is about 1000 times the saturation magnetostriction of nickel; 2.5 K of heating strains nickel as much as magnetic saturation.
description: Hydride misfit strain is a few percent, three orders of magnitude above the magnetostriction of nickel.
notes: The figure −34e-6 is the mid-value of −33 (computed from single-crystal constants) and −35 (measured, as-cast).

observed_text: When the α and β phases stay lattice-coherent the coherency strain is a macroscopic energy barrier between them, proportional to the sample volume; it cannot be crossed by thermal fluctuation unless the particle is small enough, and it produces hysteresis between absorption and desorption pressures.
implied_text: The hydride transition carries a barrier with the form of KV. It acts at the plateau pressure of a hydride former and is not a property of trapped hydrogen.
description: The barrier of a coherent hydride transformation is proportional to the transforming volume.
notes: Model statement; its measured consequence is the size dependence of the hysteresis in Pd nanocrystals. The 2006 paper applying the model to metal–hydrogen systems was not opened.

observed_text: Deuterium in Pd is bound at 0.31 eV (bubbles, vacancy clusters), 0.23 eV (single vacancy) and 0.15 eV (vacancy at high occupancy); a vacancy holds up to six atoms and binding falls after the second. bcc iron: dislocation strain field 12–27, grain boundary 9–49, single vacancy 24–78 kJ/mol. A trap deeper than 50 kJ/mol is called irreversible at room temperature.
implied_text: The barrier that holds trapped hydrogen is an energy per atom at a defect site. It does not grow with the number of atoms held; it falls as the site fills.
description: Trapped hydrogen is held by a per-atom binding energy of 0.1–0.8 eV that decreases with site occupancy.
notes: No measured trap energy for nickel was read in an opened document. value_si is 50 kJ/mol per atom.

observed_text: Pd–H is a first-order transition with hysteresis: α below x = 0.017, β above 0.58 at room temperature (tertiary); plateau 2.0 kPa for H2 and 9.8 kPa for D2 at 298 K from measured van 't Hoff constants; two-phase region closes at 566 K.
implied_text: Below the plateau pressure the dense phase does not form. Above the critical temperature there is no plateau and no hysteresis.
description: Hydride formation in palladium is a first-order transition at a plateau pressure of about 2 kPa at room temperature.
value_text: p_plateau(298 K) ≈ 2.0 kPa (H2), 9.8 kPa (D2); Tc = 566 K
notes: Phase limits rest on a tertiary page; the primary phase-diagram assessment was not opened. Plateau values are computed here from published constants.

observed_text: Nickel hydride forms at 25 °C above 6 kbar of H2, nearly stoichiometric, and decomposes near 3.4 kbar (secondary, after Baranowski). In a diamond cell nickel powder converted above about 1 GPa. Lattice parameter 3.731 Å against 3.5238 Å: 5.9 % linear, 18.7 % volume.
implied_text: Under gas below a few kilobar nickel stays a dilute solid solution. A 300 bar vessel is a factor of 20 below the formation pressure.
description: Nickel forms a hydride at room temperature only above about 6 kbar of hydrogen.
notes: The primary reference was not opened. A diamond-cell study places the conversion above about 1 GPa.

observed_text: Dilute lattice concentration follows c = S0 exp(−Es/RT) √p. Computed from measured fits at 1 bar, 298 K (extrapolated): H/Ni 1.8e-5, H/Fe 5.7e-8, H/Cu 2.3e-9. Nickel at 20, 50 and 300 bar: 8.0e-5, 1.3e-4, 3.1e-4 (5.3 wt ppm). Pd at 1 atm holds 0.68.
implied_text: Occupancy of a non-hydride-forming metal falls continuously with pressure and temperature. There is no critical pressure.
description: Lattice hydrogen in nickel, iron and copper is parts per million and scales as the square root of pressure.
value_text: H/Ni = 1.8e-5 at 1 bar; 3.1e-4 at 300 bar (298 K)
notes: Room-temperature values are extrapolated from fits made above 500 K; no fugacity correction. A tertiary source gives 2.9e-5 for nickel.

observed_text: Detrapping is thermally activated: dx/dt = A(1−x) exp(−Ea/RT), Ea = Eb + Es, with Ea read from the shift of a thermal-desorption peak with heating rate. Baking at 200 °C for 10 min removed the hydrogen from one hot-stamped steel. Smaller specimens retain less hydrogen.
implied_text: A trapped population is erased continuously with temperature and time; the 50 kJ/mol line between reversible and irreversible traps is a room-temperature convention.
description: Trapped hydrogen leaves by Arrhenius release, with no critical temperature.
notes: Peak assignment to a defect type is often uncertain. value_si is the quoted bake temperature.

observed_text: Single Pd nanocrystals: the absorption branch of the hydride hysteresis depends on size below 30 nm and the desorption branch does not; transitions are abrupt above 15 nm and sloped below. Fitted to the collected data, Tc(L) = 566 − 2381/L K, shell and core volumes are equal at 9.7 nm, and desorption is fully coherent only below about 50 nm. No hydride forms below 2.6 nm (tertiary).
implied_text: The hydride transition has two length scales in palladium: about 10 nm, where the surface shell dominates, and 30–50 nm, below which the transformation stays coherent. Dilute solubility and trapping have no minimum size.
description: The hydride transition of palladium changes character below 30–50 nm and is suppressed below a few nanometres.
notes: Measured for Pd only. No size series for nickel was found. value_si is the 30 nm figure.

observed_text: Collision time λ/v̄ = 1.4e-10 s in ambient air (λ = 66 nm, v̄ = 471 m/s for N2 at 293.15 K), longer as 1/P when rarefied.
implied_text: A gauge that resolves individual hits, or a drive faster than local equilibration, sees a shot sequence rather than P.
description: Wall pressure is an average over the impact / collision window.
notes: An ambient-air value, not a universal clock.

observed_text: QSA does not derive k or the molecular collision cross-section. The Knudsen buffer is relative (λ/L), not a fixed length.
implied_text: Both k and molecular size are taken from the descriptive relations and from sizes measured elsewhere.
description: The relative path buffer is located; k and d are not derived. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
value_text: k and d taken; no universal L
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: A dilute gas exerts a steady wall load P = nkT. At 273.15 K and 101.325 kPa n = 2.686780e25 m⁻³ (Loschmidt constant, exact).
implied_text: The stable output is the averaged wall load P = nkT and, when Kn is small, a continuum hydrodynamic field built from that average.
description: Ideal-gas pressure is the averaged momentum transfer of a thermal population onto a wall.
notes: k is exact. P = nkT and continuum hydrodynamics are different outputs; this entry owns the wall load and the Knudsen crossover.

observed_text: P = nkT is an equation of state of a dilute gas; the operating resources are density, an equilibration window and an apparatus larger than λ.
implied_text: Pressure is averaged momentum flux, not a stored configuration.
description: Ideal-gas pressure has no energy barrier that stores a state.
value_text: no latch; n, window, L ≫ λ
notes: Ionization removes the neutral population this envelope assumes. Cross-cite ionization-threshold.

observed_text: Scatter of a count N is N^{-1/2}: 0.02 % for the 2.7e7 molecules of a cubic micrometre, 1.2 % for the 7e3 in a cube of side λ.
implied_text: Same 1/√N count buffer as the temperature entry, now on the wall-load average.
description: Too few independent impacts and the pressure reading is scatter, not P = nkT.
notes: Crossover. Cross-cite thermal-equilibrium-temperature. Virial corrections at high density are a different departure.

observed_text: The continuum field degrades with Kn = λ/L through slip (0.01–0.1) and transitional flow (0.1–10) to free-molecular flow (above 10). The band edges are empirical and problem-dependent.
implied_text: As L falls toward λ, or n is lowered until λ approaches L, the local P field and sound are lost over about three decades of Kn. A free-molecular gas still delivers a time-averaged wall force.
description: The continuum reading degrades as the apparatus stops being large compared with the mean free path.
notes: Crossover. The first version put the collapse at Kn ≳ 1; the standard bands put free-molecular flow above 10. Speed of sound owns the continuum mode.

observed_text: Poisson scatter of a count N is N^{-1/2}. A cubic micrometre of gas at the Loschmidt density holds 2.7e7 molecules (0.02 %); a cube of side λ in ambient air holds about 7e3 (1.2 %).
implied_text: P as a stable reading requires enough independent impacts in the gauge window that the mean is not scatter-dominated.
description: The count buffer is statistical and continuous in 1/√N. It is a separate limit from the Knudsen crossover.
value_text: count scatter ∼ N^{-1/2}; no universal N
notes: 6.6e3 to 7.9e3 over λ = 64–68 nm.

observed_text: Kn = λ/L. Conventional bands: continuum below 0.01, slip 0.01–0.1, transitional 0.1–10, free-molecular above 10. λ = 64–68 nm in ambient air and scales as 1/n: 67 µm at 100 Pa, 6.7 mm at 1 Pa.
implied_text: A continuum P(r) requires L ≫ λ. That length tracks density; it is tens of nanometres in ambient air and millimetres at 1 Pa. It is not a material constant.
description: The spatial buffer is relative (λ/L) and moves with density.
notes: The band edges are an empirical convention. λ is not a fixed hardware length.

observed_text: No opening time is filed; no opened source gives one. The standard description puts photoionization on the optical cycle of the photon and electron-impact ionization on the collision time. Recombination is the closing clock of the ionized state.
implied_text: Opening latency is not a laboratory clock. Recombination is decay of the output, not the gate.
description: The conversion, when allowed, is already complete on any laboratory clock.
notes: No numerical opening time is given; do not invent a cycle period from the Lyman limit. No source was opened for this clause.

observed_text: QSA takes I from the database. For hydrogen and He+ the database value is calculated and is the closed description; for many-electron species the number is measured.
implied_text: Many-electron I is taken, not derived from a more primitive node rule. The collapse E < I does not depend on that derivation.
description: Hydrogen’s ladder is closed by the Rydberg formula; other species’ I is a measured specification.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Individual determinations of the H2 onset spread over 0.6 eV by method while the spectroscopic values agree to 0.3 meV.

observed_text: A species-specific series limit at I, with a free-charge yield that turns on there. For H the Lyman limit hc/I is 91.175 nm.
implied_text: A species-specific series limit and a free-charge yield that turns on at I, plus whatever plasma or chemical sequels the freed charges support.
description: The machine’s stable product is the ionization limit plus the above-threshold free-charge yield. Remove the drive and the charges return.
notes: The ionized population is not a latched state. No source was opened for the convergence of the Rydberg series on I.

observed_text: First ionization energies: H 13.598434599702 eV and He+ 54.4177655282 eV (calculated values in the NIST database); He 24.587389011 eV and H2 15.42593 ± 0.00005 eV (measured). The Lyman limit hc/I is 91.175 nm.
implied_text: I is the load-bearing gate. Photons, projectiles, or a thermal tail are interchangeable opening resources for that one barrier.
description: Ionization is the cleanest single-node photoelectric-class energy gate. Not a latch; the electron leaves.
notes: value_si is hydrogen, a calculated database value; He 24.587 eV and H2 15.426 eV are measured and sit in the same tens-of-eV class. Pair production is rest-mass creation and must not be folded into I.

observed_text: An atom already stripped of that electron has lost that gate; a deeper one may remain. Helium: 24.587 eV for the first electron, 54.418 eV for the second.
implied_text: Missing hardware closes that named ionization step. Multi-electron atoms are a ladder of gates, not one reusable cliff.
description: An already-empty valence slot cannot open I of that charge state.
value_text: electron already stripped; deeper I may remain
notes: Inner-shell rungs are filed as x-ray-absorption-edge.

observed_text: A photon or projectile with less than I does not ionize the species from its ground state. The measured optical limits are 24.587389011 eV for He and 15.42593 eV for H2; the Lyman limit of H is 91.175 nm.
implied_text: Under-threshold photon or projectile energy is the non-occurrence of the conversion. The thermal case is a separate crossover on the Saha form, with no critical temperature.
description: Below I the gas stays neutral in this channel.
notes: Thermal opening follows T^(3/2) exp(−I/kT): kT = 0.02585 eV at 300 K, I/kT = 526 for hydrogen, I/k = 1.58e5 K. The first version listed it with the photon and projectile cases as one cliff.

observed_text: One atom or molecule is the hardware for one conversion: the ionization energy is the energy to remove one electron from the ground state of one species. Helium shows two successive gates of one atom, 24.587 eV and 54.418 eV.
implied_text: A macroscopic ionized gas is the summed output of a large population. Density enters later as recombination, screening, and avalanches — sequels, not the gate.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the gate is single-particle.
notes: Dielectric-breakdown owns the many-body field avalanche that uses this gate as a step.

observed_text: Two clocks: observation bandwidth Δf, and kT/h (6.25 THz at 300 K, 83 GHz at 4 K, 21 GHz at 1 K). Above a cutoff of order kT/h the spectrum decays exponentially.
implied_text: Narrowing Δf is a longer average and kills the integrated variance. Drive or observation above kT/h leaves the classical Nyquist formula for the high-frequency envelope.
description: Classical 4kTR is an averaging-window statement below kT/h.
value_text: Δf; kT/h (6.25 THz at 300 K; 83 GHz at 4 K)
notes: h and k are defined. 6.25 THz is arithmetic, not an extracted machine clock. Ordinary audio and RF sit far below kT/h at 300 K; cryogenic microwave work does not.

observed_text: The mapping supplies no resistor volume. The zero-point term has been observed in shunted Josephson junctions; what a given amplifier can extract from it is outside this entry.
implied_text: The high-frequency form is kept as a descriptive envelope; the zero-point contribution is recorded as measured and not assigned a machine role.
description: No volume threshold is extracted, and zero-point voltage is not filed as a QSA output.
value_text: no volume threshold; zero-point observed, not mapped
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: ⟨V²⟩ = 4kTRΔf (one-sided). At 300 K: 4.07 nV/√Hz for 1 kΩ and 0.91 nV/√Hz for 50 Ω. Johnson's measurements gave a Boltzmann constant near the accepted value.
implied_text: A white voltage floor 4kTR is the electrical average of the thermal population, with a definite integrated variance once Δf is stated.
description: The stable output is the Nyquist floor, the electrical counterpart of D = kT/γ.
notes: k is exact. The nV/√Hz figures are arithmetic at 300 K.

observed_text: Voltage noise is proportional to R; the same Langevin equation as Brownian motion with C for m and 1/R for γ. Nothing is stored.
implied_text: Noise is the electrical average of a dissipative element, not a stored configuration.
description: Johnson–Nyquist has no energy barrier that stores a state.
notes: Cross-cite superconductivity for the R→0 realization.

observed_text: Integrated variance 4kTRΔf is proportional to Δf.
implied_text: Lengthen the average until the variance is gone. That is the family clock failure run on the filter.
description: Vanishing bandwidth collapses the integrated Nyquist variance.
notes: Crossover, linear in Δf.

observed_text: Voltage noise is proportional to R and current noise to 1/R.
implied_text: Remove the dissipative resource and the voltage floor collapses.
description: A short, including a superconductor, has no Johnson voltage noise.
notes: Crossover in R; a superconducting transition makes it a threshold in temperature for that material (superconductivity). Skin effect changes the R(f) used.

observed_text: Classical ⟨V²⟩ = 4kTRΔf is proportional to T. A zero-point contribution has been observed at high frequency in shunted Josephson junctions.
implied_text: Shrink the thermal resource and the classical electrical average falls in proportion.
description: Classical Johnson noise collapses as T→0.
notes: Crossover, linear in T. Shares this with brownian-motion.

observed_text: The Nyquist value 4kTRΔf depends only on T, R and Δf. Shot noise is a separate output that follows from charge quantization and needs a current.
implied_text: The hardware is a dissipative element with stable R, coupled to a thermal population with stable T, averaged over the chosen Δf. Inventing a minimum N of carriers would be a conjecture.
description: Johnson–Nyquist names a statistical average and attaches no resistor volume.
notes: No measurement on nanometre-scale resistors was opened; that statement is mapping language only.

observed_text: Josephson constant K_J = 2e/h = 483 597.848 4… GHz/V, exact since the 2019 SI: 483.6 MHz per microvolt.
implied_text: The AC Josephson lock is the clock: a microvolt bias oscillates at hundreds of megahertz; a millivolt bias sits in the sub-terahertz. This is a frequency locked to a voltage, not a plasma-period screening cycle.
description: The weak-link clock is 483.6 MHz per microvolt of DC bias.
notes: value_si is Hz per volt. Shapiro steps are the same clock read out against an external microwave drive.

observed_text: The measured charge increment in h/2e is taken from the voltage-frequency lock and from the flux quantum.
implied_text: QSA does not derive why the increment is 2e rather than e from node rules alone. That increment is recorded as data. No pairing story is required to locate the collapses, and none is added.
description: The 2e in h/2e is located as a measured increment, not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; the open item is the origin of the increment, not the location of the collapses. RSJ C and R are descriptive bookkeeping.

observed_text: V = (h/2e)ν with 2e/h = 483 597.848 4… GHz/V; under microwave irradiation at f the steps sit at V_n = n h f/2e (20.7 μV spacing at 10 GHz).
implied_text: The synchronized output is a universal voltage-frequency lock V = (h/2e) ν once a voltage is present, together with a dissipationless weak-link current at V=0 for |I| ≤ Ic.
description: The Josephson machine emits a metrological V–ν lock at 2e/h, and a zero-voltage supercurrent below Ic.
notes: Complementary metrological lock to quantum-hall-effect (RK = h/e²).

observed_text: Ic is set by the junction (area, barrier transparency, electrode gap) and is not a universal constant. A DC supercurrent exists only for |I| ≤ Ic.
implied_text: Ic is the current threshold that protects the zero-voltage branch. The electrode gap is the energy scale that vanishes at Tc and takes Ic with it.
description: The zero-voltage branch is gated by a junction-specific Ic, not by a universal current.
notes: A flux of order Φ0 through the junction is a field threshold that suppresses Ic without first destroying the electrodes.

observed_text: Above Ic a finite DC voltage appears across the link. For |I| > Ic the junction is on a resistive branch and V ≠ 0.
implied_text: Current over-budget ends the zero-voltage branch. The voltage-frequency lock can then run; the dissipationless DC current is gone.
description: Crossing Ic collapses the V=0 supercurrent.
notes: T > Tc in either electrode is a coarser collapse: the parent condensate is gone. Electrode Hc / Hc2 is owned by superconductivity / type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: A flux of order Φ0 = 2.067 833 848…×10⁻¹⁵ Wb through the junction area modulates Ic in a diffraction pattern with zeros at integer multiples of Φ0.
implied_text: A flux of order Φ0 is a field threshold that suppresses Ic without first destroying the electrodes.
description: Junction-scale flux of one quantum collapses Ic by interference, not by driving the electrodes normal.
notes: The diffraction pattern is cited to Rowell (1963), not opened. Φ0 is exact.

observed_text: The oxide barrier of a working Al junction is about 1 to 2 nm, and the thinnest tenth of its area carries most of the current, so the critical current falls steeply and continuously with thickness.
implied_text: A thicker insulator weakens the coupling continuously and the weak-link current falls toward zero.
description: A thicker or more opaque barrier is the spatial failure of the Josephson machine; a crossover in thickness.
notes: No decay length filed; the steep dependence is inferred from the dominance of the thinnest regions.

observed_text: In Al/AlOx/Al junctions the oxide barrier is about 1 to 2 nm thick with a Gaussian spread, and less than 10 % of the barrier area dominates the tunnelling.
implied_text: Two nested buffers: each electrode must be a superconducting condensate, and they must be coupled by a weak link whose thickness sits in a narrow window. The load-bearing node of this artifact is the phase difference φ across that under-coupled spatial buffer.
description: The Josephson machine is a weak link, 1–2 nm of oxide in a tunnel junction, between two parent condensates; a thicker barrier carries less current.
notes: value_si is the middle of the measured 1–2 nm range. With no barrier the two sides are one superconductor with no junction degree of freedom. Electrode Tc, ξ and gap are owned by superconductivity.

observed_text: Precession scale γ/2π = 28.025 GHz/T (CODATA 2022). Near the coercive field wall motion is the dominant magnetization mechanism, and Barkhausen jumps are irregular fluctuations in the motion of a wall.
implied_text: A static pattern has no ongoing clock cost. Pattern changes are wall-motion events that proceed in unpinning jumps set by the defect structure.
description: Domain walls inherit the 28 GHz/T spin carrier; the partition itself changes in pinning-limited jumps.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency. No wall velocity is filed. Damping and eddy currents, named in the first version as limits on wall speed, had no opened source and were dropped.

observed_text: Why one sample shows closure domains, another stripes, another a maze is a magnetostatic-plus-pinning problem. A and K1 are taken as inputs to the wall width and energy; A is inferred, and two tabulations differ by 2.4×. In soft material the coercive field is the field at which walls unpin from defects.
implied_text: QSA does not produce A and K1 from a more primitive buffer, and does not select the imaged pattern from node rules. The mesoscale Hc gap reappears as pinning.
description: Pattern choice and the pinning that sets technical Hc remain mesoscale data; the finite wall width and the single-domain crossover do not depend on closing them.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason.

observed_text: Walls are imaged by Bitter powder patterns, electron microscopy, Kerr microscopy and magnetic force microscopy. In zero applied field the net moment can be far below saturation even though each domain is locally ordered; at saturation the body is one domain.
implied_text: Stable output is a static partition of the aligned population, with walls of finite width and a net moment set by how closed the pattern is.
description: Domains emit a held partition, not a requirement of a large net dipole.
notes: The measured wall width in Nd2Fe14B is 4–9 nm.

observed_text: Holding a static domain pattern costs zero continuous power: it is a static configuration, and no source reports a dissipation at rest.
implied_text: Hold-power of a static partition is zero. Wall motion around a hysteresis loop dissipates the loop area.
description: Holding a domain pattern costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when walls move.

observed_text: Wall energy by the Bloch formula 4√(A·K1): 2.6 mJ/m² (Fe), 9.3 (Co), 0.5 (Ni), 5.7 (BaFe12O19), 25 (Nd2Fe14B), 77 (SmCo5). A second tabulation gives 1.2 (Fe), 9 (BaFe12O19), 27 (Nd2Fe14B) and 120 (SmCo5). Holding a static domain pattern costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Each domain is the parent anisotropy latch. The wall is a distributed transition whose energy per area is the price of a partition. Pinning of walls at defects is the barrier that appears as Hc in soft material.
description: Partition cost is wall area times 4√(A·K1), 0.5–77 mJ/m² in the tabulation; static patterns have no hold-power bill.
value_text: γ_w = 0.5–77 mJ/m² (Nd2Fe14B 25); zero hold-power at rest
notes: value_si is Nd2Fe14B. The two tabulations differ by 2.2× for Fe, 1.6× for BaFe12O19 and SmCo5, and 1.1× for Nd2Fe14B.

observed_text: Magnetization proceeds by wall motion and by rotation inside the domains. In iron and Fe–Si walls unpin at the coercive field (10–100 A/m in polycrystalline iron) and substantial rotation needs 10^3–10^4 A/m. No opened source gives a saturation field or reports saturation as a sharp transition.
implied_text: An applied field expels the walls and the partition is gone; the local latch remains. The field that removes the last wall is microstructure-dependent.
description: Saturation removes the domain pattern and leaves the local directional latch; it is a crossover with no single field.
value_text: walls displaced at Hc; rotation at 10^3–10^4 A/m (Fe, Fe–Si)
notes: T > Tc removes local order and therefore domains (a threshold). Grain-scale relaxation is superparamagnetism.

observed_text: Single-domain diameter by 72√(A·K1)/(μ0·Ms²): 12 nm (Fe), 68 nm (Co), 32 nm (Ni), 580 nm (BaFe12O19), 214 nm (Nd2Fe14B), 1528 nm (SmCo5). Micromagnetic calculations give 25 nm for iron cubes. Measured for Nd2Fe14B: about 0.2–0.4 µm. Kittel's first estimates were movable by a factor of ten.
implied_text: Below the single-domain size the pattern does not form and the particle is one latch cell. The size is an energy comparison with a shape-dependent prefactor.
description: The domain pattern gives way to a single domain at a material-dependent size: a crossover running from 12–25 nm in iron to 0.2–1.5 µm in hard magnets.
notes: value_si is the Fe diameter. The prefactor is 72 for a diameter and 36 for a radius. For Fe and Ni the tabulated room-temperature blocking diameter (16 and 34 nm) lies above the tabulated single-domain diameter (12 and 31 nm); the 25 nm micromagnetic value for iron would leave a window of 16–25 nm.

observed_text: Wall width measured in Nd2Fe14B: no wider than 7 and 9 nm (90° and 180° walls) by electron holography, about 6 nm by neutron scattering, 4–9 nm by other methods. By the Bloch formula π√(A/K1) the tabulated widths are 40 nm (Fe), 14 nm (Co), 82 nm (Ni), 3.9 nm (Nd2Fe14B) and 3.6 nm (SmCo5). No direct measurement was found for bulk Fe, Co or Ni.
implied_text: The wall is a finite-width spatial buffer in which the moment rotates between adjacent latched directions.
description: A domain wall is a transition strip of finite width: 4–9 nm measured in Nd2Fe14B, 3.6–82 nm by formula across the tabulated materials.
notes: value_si is the Nd2Fe14B neutron-scattering value. The formula widths are Model: exchange stiffness is inferred and two tabulations differ by 2.4×, which moves a width by 1.55×. The first version's sentence that two domains merge below the wall width had no source and was removed.

observed_text: No clock of its own. Magnetic side: the domain-wall and rotation clocks of the magnet entries. Mechanical side: the acoustic transit of elasticity.
implied_text: The length-change clock is the magnet’s write / wall motion plus acoustic transit, not the Larmor carrier.
description: No separate magnetostrictive period is extracted. Lab loops are sweep- and wall-limited.
value_text: magnet clocks + acoustic transit; none of its own
notes: No source opened on dynamic or cyclic magnetostriction.

observed_text: Why λ_s is 4×10⁻⁵ in nickel and 10⁻³ in Terfenol-D is taken as data, the same way d_33 is taken as data on piezoelectricity.
implied_text: The T_C and lattice-destruction collapses are located; λ_s is a handbook coupling.
description: Coupling magnitude is taken, not derived from a stated node-level spring. Mapping confidence is therefore medium.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch: do not re-specify remanence, T_C, or KV here.

observed_text: Room temperature: nickel −35 to −40 ppm polycrystalline (λ100 −46, λ111 −24); iron −9 ppm (λ100 20, λ111 −21); Galfenol about 400 ppm; Terfenol-D 1000–2000 ppm depending on field and prestress (λ100 90, λ111 1640).
implied_text: A saturation strain λ_s locked to the aligned moment, plus the inverse stress–M channel, while the ordered magnet and the lattice both remain.
description: The strain output is a material number from −9 ppm (Fe) and −40 ppm (Ni) to 400 ppm (Galfenol) and above 1000 ppm (Terfenol-D), fixed to the axis of the moment.
value_text: Ni −33 to −40 ppm; Fe −9; Galfenol 400; Terfenol-D 1000–2000 ppm
notes: Joule strain conserves volume; volume magnetostriction is separate. The whole strain of nickel equals the thermal expansion from a 2.6–3.0 K rise.

observed_text: No separate magnetostrictive latch. The thresholds are the host magnet's: the Curie point (nickel 631 K) and the field that aligns the moment (nickel [100]: 300 Oe internal). The elastic energy of a clamped 35 ppm strain in nickel is 122 J m⁻³, equal to a temperature rise of 3.1×10⁻⁵ K.
implied_text: This file must not re-specify the magnet. Strain is locked to M; the barrier that holds M is the latch’s.
description: Magnetostriction is a coupling, not a latch. T_C, KV, and coercivity stay with permanent-magnet-latch.
value_text: T_C 631 K (Ni); 300 Oe internal; ½Eλ² = 122 J/m³
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch. The inverse (Villari) effect is measured: stress changes the magnetization.

observed_text: The saturation strain falls to zero at the Curie point: nickel 631 K (358–360 °C), iron 1042 K. Below it the strain falls continuously with the magnetization, most steeply close to the transition; nickel λ100 is −57 to −60 ppm near 0 K and −46 ppm at room temperature.
implied_text: T > T_C → ordered moment gone → λ = 0. This file owns the length change, not the latch.
description: Magnetostriction dies at the host Curie point with the ordered moment.
notes: value_si is the nickel Curie point. Terfenol-D Curie temperature not found; Galfenol 700 °C.

observed_text: Melting removes the solid. No opened source supports shock scrambling a magnet through this coupling. The full saturation strain of nickel, clamped, gives 7.0–8.8 MPa, which is 4.3–5.4 % of the 163 MPa yield constant of Nickel 200; the elastic strain at yield is 23 times the magnetostrictive strain.
implied_text: No lattice, no strain. Magnetostrictive stress in nickel is about a twentieth of yield, so this coupling does not by itself produce plastic damage.
description: Lattice loss is melting. Static magnetostrictive stress in nickel is far below yield.
notes: Corrected: the first version treated shock through this coupling as a mechanical failure path. Cyclic loading not sourced.

observed_text: The strain follows M(H) and saturates. Nickel [100] saturates at an internal field of 300 Oe; a 5:1 ellipsoid needed 650 Oe applied, and an isolated sphere needs about 0.23 T. Composition can remove the coupling: 7 at.% Ga takes nickel from −35 to −10 ppm.
implied_text: Macroscopic ΔL is small if M is not aligned, even when λ_s is finite. Alignment is a domain / coercivity condition, not a second coupling.
description: Below saturation the macroscopic strain is partial. The applied field needed depends on shape through the demagnetizing factor.
value_text: 300 Oe internal (Ni); ~0.23 T applied for a sphere
notes: Cross-cite magnetic-domains and ferromagnetic-hysteresis. The strain is even in M: reversal leaves it unchanged.

observed_text: An ordered magnetic population in a deformable lattice. A body free to deform takes up the strain with no stress; when the deformation is hindered a stress λ_s E/(1+ν) appears instead: 5.3 MPa in nickel, or Eλ_s = 7.0–8.8 MPa for a bar held at both ends.
implied_text: Hardware is ordered M plus a strain-carrying grid. Grain-scale latching of M is owned by permanent-magnet-latch / superparamagnetism; this file owns the strain that follows M.
description: Magnetostriction needs an ordered moment and a deformable lattice. Stress appears only under constraint and is 5–9 MPa in nickel.
value_text: ordered M + deformable lattice; clamped stress 5–9 MPa (Ni)
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch. A free particle changes shape without stress.

observed_text: Expulsion on cooling through Tc is limited by thermal diffusion, eddy-current transients, and (in type II) flux-line motion — laboratory times, not the gap frequency 2Δ/h.
implied_text: This entry's static observation is the ω=0 expelled state. The gap frequency still sets the scale on which the condensate can respond to a changing field.
description: Static Meissner expulsion is not a 2Δ/h clock measurement; the expelled state is already the DC output.
notes: Contrast with josephson-effect, which owns the voltage-frequency lock.

observed_text: Cooling in a field yields B=0 rather than freeze-in. A hypothetical perfect conductor would trap the flux it already contained, not expel it. λ is a measured screening length, not a derived node count.
implied_text: QSA records expulsion as the stable output of the gapped state; it does not yet produce expulsion-versus-trapping from a more primitive update rule, and it takes λ as the hardware depth.
description: Why the equilibrium is expulsion rather than flux trapping is located as data, not derived from node rules. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Same kind of underived screening length as the optical decay length λ/4πk on reflection.

observed_text: A superconducting element such as lead expels a weak magnetic field from its interior when cooled below Tc; the bulk field vanishes behind a surface layer of depth λ.
implied_text: A field-free interior behind a surface layer of depth λ is the stable output of a fully provisioned screening buffer.
description: Complete Meissner expulsion is perfect diamagnetism of the expelled volume, held at zero continuous power.
notes: This entry owns field expulsion / λ. Superconductivity owns R=0.

observed_text: Type I: no field in the bulk below Hc (Al 10 mT, Sn 30.5 mT, Pb 80.3 mT). Type II: complete expulsion below Hc1 (Nb ≈ 160 mT at 2 K).
implied_text: Hc (type I) and Hc1 (type II) are the load-bearing field gates for complete expulsion. Holding the expelled state costs no continuous power.
description: Complete field expulsion is gated by Hc or Hc1, not by a static anisotropy latch.
value_text: H < Hc (type I; Pb 80.3 mT) or H < Hc1 (type II; Nb 160 mT)
notes: value_si is Pb μ0 Hc. Type-II Hc1 and the mixed state are owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: Above Hc (type I) the field enters and superconductivity ends; above Hc1 (type II) the field enters as flux tubes of one Φ0 while zero resistance can persist to Hc2. Pb 80.3 mT; Nb Bc1 ≈ 160 mT, Bc2 ≈ 300 mT at 2 K.
implied_text: Crossing the complete-expulsion gate is a Meissner failure even when the R=0 channel is still open.
description: The Meissner artifact dies at Hc or Hc1; that is not the same collapse as R=0.
value_text: H > Hc (type I) or H > Hc1 (type II)
notes: Split from superconductivity is required by the type-II mixed state. Hc2 is owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: Expulsion appears on cooling below Tc and ends on warming through it; the critical fields fall to zero at Tc.
implied_text: Thermal closure of the parent gap sends the screening depth to infinity and the expelled state disappears.
description: Expulsion ends at Tc with the parent condensate.
notes: Material Tc values are tabulated on superconductivity. Type-I intermediate state from a finite demagnetizing factor is a shape-dependent partition, not a second condensate.

observed_text: In a sheet thinner than λ the field does not fall to zero at the centre and the sheet's critical field can be much larger than that of a thick slab; it remains superconducting. London slab: mid-plane field B0/cosh(d/2λ), 0.89 B0 at d = λ, 0.43 B0 at 3λ, 0.013 B0 at 10λ. One-atomic-layer Pb and In films superconduct.
implied_text: Screening weakens continuously as the body thins; there is no thickness at which expulsion switches off, and superconductivity is not lost at d = λ.
description: Expulsion is incomplete in a body thinner than a few λ; a crossover, not a minimum thickness.
notes: value_si is λ for Pb. The monolayer result rests on a snippet.

observed_text: Tabulated penetration depth: Al 16 nm, Sn 50 nm, Pb 40 nm, Nb 85 nm; a second table gives Pb 32 nm, Sn about 30 nm, Nb 32 nm (typical range 20–50 nm). YBCO: λa 103 nm, λb 80 nm, λc 635 nm. The field decays as exp(−x/λ) into a flat surface.
implied_text: λ is the e-folding depth of the field. A body several λ thick has a field-free interior; a thinner body screens partially and still superconducts.
description: Complete expulsion needs a screening buffer of tens of nanometres in conventional elements, of order 100 nm in YBCO's ab plane.
notes: value_si is Pb, 40 nm. The two opened tables differ by a factor of 2.7 for Nb. λ is not a minimum thickness for superconductivity.

observed_text: Melting is limited by heat supply and by nucleation at a surface. Gold-coated silver spheres of about 130 µm stayed solid at least 7.5 K above the melting point of silver for about one minute; without a coating superheating is a few degrees or less.
implied_text: The conversion clock is heat supply and surface nucleation; no material clock is filed.
description: Melting starts at a surface; with the surface blocked a crystal can be held above T_m for about a minute.
value_text: nucleation-limited; ≥ 7.5 K superheat for ~1 min (coated Ag)
notes: The comparison with Debye temperatures (Pb, diamond) was dropped: no opened source.

observed_text: Lindemann criterion: melting when the rms displacement reaches about one tenth of the interatomic distance; it is not very accurately fulfilled. Reported ratios span 0.12–0.19 (0.15–0.16 fcc, 0.18–0.19 bcc) and are not universal.
implied_text: QSA takes measured T_m as the empirical threshold. Lindemann is a displacement consistency check, not a derived barrier.
description: The mapping does not close on why a metal melts at its particular temperature. Lindemann is a rule of thumb, not a node-level derivation.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium while T_m data are High. Cohesive well depth, coordination, and anharmonicity (thermal-expansion) enter and are not yet primitive node specifications. Soft-mode melting belongs with phonon-dispersion. value_si is the 0.1–0.15 window midpoint.

observed_text: A material constant T_m(P), reproducible to about 0.1 mK in pure metals used as temperature fixed points (Sn 505.078 K, Zn 692.677 K, Al 933.473 K, Cu 1357.77 K), and a fixed enthalpy of fusion: Cu 13.14, Al 10.71, Fe 13.81, Ni 17.16, Zn 7.32 kJ mol⁻¹.
implied_text: The stable product is the coexistence temperature itself plus the solid/fluid sides of the cliff.
description: The output is a solid below T_m and a first-order conversion at a reproducible temperature with a fixed latent heat.
notes: Pressure slope 3.3–7.0 K per kbar (Sn, Zn, Al).

observed_text: Melting points at one atmosphere: Zn 692.73 K, Al 933.45 K, Cu 1358 K, Ni 1728 K, Fe 1809 K; W 3660–3695 K. Enthalpy of fusion: Cu 207, Al 397, Fe 247, Ni 292, Zn 112 kJ kg⁻¹. From 300 K to fully liquid: Cu 673, Al 1062, Fe 1297, Ni 1098, Zn 277 kJ kg⁻¹ (6.03, 2.87, 10.21, 9.78, 1.97 GJ m⁻³).
implied_text: Two numbers per material: the temperature T_m and the enthalpy of fusion. Reaching T_m is not sufficient; fusion is 19–40 % of the heat needed from room temperature.
description: T_m and the enthalpy of fusion are measured gates of the lattice, not derived barriers.
notes: value_si left null: several pins. Enthalpies computed from NIST-JANAF entries; tin estimated at about 109 kJ/kg.

observed_text: Order can also be lost below T_m by heavy plastic strain, irradiation or dissolution. No source was opened and no measured scale is filed.
implied_text: Those are lattice-destruction routes, not the thermal coexistence cliff.
description: Plastic strain, radiation, or dissolution can erase the grid without reaching T_m.
notes: Unsourced statement kept as a named route. Latch entries may list lattice loss as a secondary failure.

observed_text: At T_m for the given pressure the solid converts to liquid with a latent heat, and the static shear modulus goes from a finite value to zero. T_m rises 3.3 (Sn), 4.3 (Zn) and 7.0 (Al) K per kilobar. A surface-coated crystal has been held 7.5 K above T_m for about a minute.
implied_text: Loss of the ordered lattice at the measured coexistence temperature. The shear wave and static shear stiffness end with the solid, in a jump.
description: The lattice fails at T_m: latent heat, G from finite to zero, one sound wave left.
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound and elasticity. No soft-mode precursor in the sources opened.

observed_text: A crystal large enough for the bulk value to hold. Gold particles down to 20 Å melt lower: 2.5 nm gold at 320 K (corrected) or about 673 K (uncorrected) against 1337 K for the bulk; 4.1 nm at 782 K and 1.6 nm at 405 K by an electrochemical transition. The depression is roughly proportional to 1/d.
implied_text: The hardware is an ordered lattice large against a few nanometres. Below that the melting temperature falls roughly as the inverse diameter.
description: Bulk melting needs a crystal much larger than a few nanometres; micrometre powder is bulk for this purpose.
value_text: bulk T_m for d ≫ nm; Au 2.5 nm: 320–673 K vs 1337 K
notes: Glasses have no crystalline order to lose; that statement is not sourced in the file.

observed_text: 57Fe 14.4 keV state: half-life 98.3(3) ns, mean life 141.8 ns, which sets Γ = 4.64 neV. The host vibration spectrum sets f.
implied_text: Nuclear lifetime plus host phonon clock.
description: Γ from nuclear τ; f from the grid clock.

observed_text: 14.4 keV is the line energy, not an under-threshold non-occurrence of this channel.
implied_text: Do not file as an energy-gate whose collapse is Eγ<14.4 keV.
description: Lattice-mode payload, not a 14.4 keV under-threshold gate.
value_text: Eγ is the line, not a threshold

observed_text: Recoilless resonant absorption in a solid host, scanned with Doppler velocities on the scale cΓ/Eγ = 0.097 mm/s for 57Fe.
implied_text: The lattice-enabled nuclear line is the output.
description: Recoilless resonance as the stable output.

observed_text: 57Fe line at 14.4129(6) keV with natural width Γ = 4.64 neV. One natural width corresponds to a Doppler velocity of 0.097 mm/s.
implied_text: Nuclear line plus lattice recoilless condition. Not an under-threshold 14.4 keV gate.
description: Overlap within Γ is the operating window.

observed_text: f = exp(−k²⟨x²⟩) falls continuously with temperature. In tin the absorption drops rapidly and the line broadens in the last few degrees below melting, assigned to self-diffusion (about 1e-8 cm²/s at 0.6 K below T_m). The effect is not achieved in ordinary liquids. Model diffusive width 2ħk²D: equal to Γ at D = 6.6e-16 m²/s for 57Fe, about 9e5 Γ at D = 0.6e-9 m²/s.
implied_text: The resonance is lost through rising ⟨x²⟩ and through diffusion, both continuous; the loss near melting begins in the solid.
description: No recoilless, narrow line once the nucleus recoils freely or diffuses within the nuclear lifetime.
value_text: f falls with T; diffusion width 2ħk²D; no resonance in gas or ordinary liquid
notes: Not a threshold at T_m. No numeric f(T) for a named host was opened.

observed_text: Recoilless emission and absorption occur in the solid state, crystalline or non-crystalline, and not for free atoms, gases or liquids. Free 57Fe has E_R = 1.96 meV against Γ = 4.64 neV (ratio 4.2e5).
implied_text: The host that binds the nucleus is the buffer; crystalline order is not required. A free atom is under-provisioned.
description: Recoilless resonance needs a binding host in which the nucleus neither recoils freely nor diffuses during the nuclear lifetime.
value_text: binding solid host (crystalline or not); not a free atom
notes: Bragg order is not the resource: non-crystalline solids support the effect.

observed_text: Muon mean life τμ = 2.1969811(22)e-6 s (PDG 2026). Cycling rate about 1e8 per second, so λc τμ ≈ 220; fusion inside a formed dtμ ion is about 1e12 per second (model).
implied_text: τμ is the stop. The cycle time (about 1e-8 s, set by atomic and molecular steps) is the clock that competes with it.
description: The catalysis clock is the muon lifetime, not a lattice attempt time.
notes: Lifetime taken from PDG 2026.

observed_text: With no muons there is no cycle; nothing is retained after the last muon decays.
implied_text: This is not a 0 W latch. Identifying it with a defect-pinned interstitial cell is a mapping error.
description: Honest exclusion: μCF is a spent-node gate, not a hold-power memory.
value_text: not 0 W hold after muon gone
notes: Contrast membership on anisotropy-latch. Does not add a nuclear effect to the latch family.

observed_text: About 150 fusions per stopped muon in cold, dense d–t (LAMPF; 150 ± 20), over 100 as the reproduced class. At 150 fusions the release is 2.64 GeV per muon against an estimated production cost of about 5 GeV electrical or 10 GeV thermal.
implied_text: Stable output is fusion-product yield per stopped muon, Y ≈ 1/(ωs + λ0/λc), only while muons are present.
description: The machine emits a per-muon fusion yield, not a remnant cell at 0 W.
notes: value_si is the LAMPF record. The production cost is an estimate (no such source built); break-even needs about 300 or more fusions per muon.

observed_text: mμ c² = 105.6583755 MeV; mμ/me = 206.7682827. The muon's orbit is smaller than the electron's by that ratio (a0/206.77 = 256 fm before reduced-mass corrections), and the internuclear distance in a muonic molecular ion is about 500 times smaller than in H2+.
implied_text: Not a latch. The muon mass shrinks the bound orbit so the nuclei fuse in about a picosecond. The product leaves; the muon is reused until it decays or sticks.
description: The gate opener is the muon mass ratio, not lattice strain and not KV.
notes: value_si is the muon rest energy. Q(dt)=17.6 MeV is the fusion release, not the gate that opens the cycle. Orbit scaling is a Bohr-model statement; the masses are measured.

observed_text: Each muon is lost by decay (e^(-t/τμ)) or by sticking to the alpha. Effective d–t sticking is 0.35–0.6 % and falls with density (0.45 % in the molecular cycle); d–d sticking in the 3He + n branch is 12.2 %. The two losses add: Y ≈ 1/(ωs + λ0/λc). At optimum the decay limit and the sticking limit are each about 300, giving about 150.
implied_text: Sticking and decay together cap the cycle. Both are continuous, per-cycle loss probabilities, not a blocking temperature.
description: Decay and sticking are additive losses that set the yield.
notes: value_si is the molecular-cycle value 0.45 % (Rafelski 1991). Sourcing replaced min(1/ωs, λcτμ) with the additive relation and corrected d–d sticking from ~10 % to 12.2 %.

observed_text: The cycle is defined by a stopped muon replacing an electron. No muon-free hydrogen target is reported to produce it.
implied_text: Missing muon is the collapse of the effect. Lattice compression and H/M do not substitute for the particle.
description: No muon ⇒ no cycle. Counterpart of pair-production’s missing recoil partner.
notes: Largely definitional. This is the contrast to any muon-free cell.

observed_text: One muon and two hydrogen-isotope nuclei form the fusing ion. Only ddμ and dtμ form by a resonant process, in which a host D2 or DT molecule takes up the 0.660 eV binding energy; non-resonant formation is slower than muon decay. No metal host is involved. The dtμ formation rate depends non-linearly on density.
implied_text: N = 1 muon + two nuclei, plus one host molecule for the fast cycle. A few-body requirement, not a collective medium. Density raises the cycle rate and lowers sticking.
description: The gate hardware is one muon, two hydrogen nuclei and a host molecule for resonant formation. Target volume is capacity.
notes: Sourced 2026-11-11: host molecule added (Cohen 1989). Same N=1 family as photoelectric, with a different particle.

observed_text: Classical bounce period of the lowest state 3.3 ms; a 10 cm mirror at 10 m/s is crossed in 10 ms, about three periods.
implied_text: Not a nuclear lifetime.
description: UCN bounce clock.

observed_text: The spacing is gravitational, not a pairing gap. No charge, no λ, no Tc.
implied_text: Do not fold into gapped-condensate. Same honesty as He-4.
description: Family name is loose; leftover, not a tenth design.

observed_text: Zero transmission through a slit lower than about 15 μm and a rise above it; the computed turning heights of the first four states are 13.7, 24.0, 32.4 and 39.8 μm.
implied_text: Discrete gravitational states as the stable output.
description: Height steps at the Airy turning points.

observed_text: Level energies 1.4, 2.5, 3.3 and 4.1 peV (computed here: 1.41, 2.46, 3.32, 4.08 peV); E1/k = 16 nK.
implied_text: Gravitational level spacing is the protecting gap. Family name gapped is loose.
description: peV gravitational ladder, not a pairing gap.
notes: value_si corrected: 1.41 peV is 2.25×10⁻³¹ J (the earlier row was a factor of 1000 high).

observed_text: A slit lower than about 15 μm is not transparent to neutrons (count rate zero, reproduced 11 times); the ideal turning height is 13.7 μm and the fitted heights sit about 3 μm above the ideal values.
implied_text: Under-height slit or wrong buffer collapses the steps.
description: z < z1 or not-UCN is the collapse.
notes: Resolved to a few micrometres; the edge is softened by the overlap with the absorber.

observed_text: Turning height of the lowest state 13.7 μm (computed, Airy solution); a slit lower than about 15 μm between mirror and absorber passes no neutrons. Horizontal velocity 5–15 m/s, vertical below 5 cm/s; mirrors 6–10 cm long.
implied_text: The spatial buffer is the height of the gravitational well above a reflecting floor.
description: A neutron with centimetre-per-second vertical speed, a horizontal mirror and g over about 14 μm is the hardware.

observed_text: No conversion time was sourced. The slowing of the pair and the annihilation of the positron are later steps.
implied_text: Annihilation witnesses the conversion; it is not the gate.
description: No conversion time was sourced.
notes: No numerical QED time is given; do not invent ħ/2mec².

observed_text: QSA takes me c² = 0.51099895069 MeV as a measured node specification. It does not derive the electron mass from a more primitive resource count.
implied_text: The collapse clauses (Eγ < 1.0220 MeV; no recoil partner) do not depend on that derivation.
description: The rest mass is located and measured; it is not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: Annihilation of a pair at rest gives two photons of mec² = 511.0 keV each.
implied_text: A material- and energy-dependent pair yield above 1.022 MeV, followed by the 511 keV annihilation line, as the synchronized output of many independent photon–nucleus conversions.
description: The machine’s stable product is a pair yield plus the 511 keV line.
notes: value_si is one 511 keV photon.

observed_text: me c² = 0.51099895069 MeV. The threshold is 2mec²(1 + me/M): 1.0220 MeV for a heavy nucleus; the recoil term adds 0.56 keV for a proton and 47 eV for ¹²C.
implied_text: The operating gate is the rest-mass sum 2me c². It is not the unbinding of a pre-existing electron. No optical photoelectric event opens this channel.
description: Pair production is a rest-mass creation gate, not an ionization gate.
notes: It is not the unbinding of an existing electron.

observed_text: A single photon has zero invariant mass and cannot convert alone at any energy. Two photons can supply the partner for each other: 6085 exclusive pairs were observed in ultra-peripheral Au+Au collisions.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning closes the channel even for Eγ > 1.022 MeV.
description: Missing recoil partner is a spatial-buffer collapse, twin of the energy threshold.
value_text: no partner (nucleus, electron or second photon)
notes: The two-photon case, an extension in the first version, is observed.

observed_text: With an electron as the partner the threshold is 4mec² = 2.0440 MeV. The tabulated electron-field coefficient in lead is zero at 2.044 MeV and 4.8e-9 cm² g⁻¹ at 2.1 MeV.
implied_text: An electron as the only recoil partner keeps the gate shut until 2.044 MeV. Same conversion, lighter momentum sink.
description: Wrong partner raises the rest-mass gate; it does not invent a second family.

observed_text: Below 1.0220 MeV there is no conversion. In lead the tabulated nuclear-field pair coefficient is zero at 1.022 MeV and 3.3e-8 cm² g⁻¹ at 1.03 MeV: the yield starts from zero with no step.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below 2mec² the pair gate stays shut.
notes: Competition with other channels is a crossover: pair production equals incoherent scattering at about 4.7 MeV in lead and 26 MeV in carbon.

observed_text: One photon and one partner that can recoil. The threshold 2mec²(1 + me/M) diverges as M → 0, so a single photon cannot convert alone. The leading cross-section term scales as Z².
implied_text: The partner is a spatial-buffer condition: the photon must pass through the field of a mass that can recoil. A photon alone is under-provisioned at every energy.
description: Hardware is one photon plus one recoil partner. The spatial clause is mandatory, not decorative.
notes: No length for 'nearby' is given. At 10 MeV the nuclear-field pair coefficient per unit mass is 9.5 times larger in lead than in carbon.

observed_text: Free-electron gyromagnetic ratio γe/2π = 28 024.951 MHz/T (CODATA 2022).
implied_text: Baseline single-spin clock of the latch. Write/erase of a hard magnet is set by field sweep and wall motion, not this carrier.
description: The latch has a 28 GHz/T precession clock; holding the state does not require running that clock as a power draw.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency.

observed_text: The first sintered magnet had coercivity 960 kA/m (about 1.2 T), 16–18 % of the 6.7–7.65 T anisotropy field. In simulation a defect-free cubic grain reaches 3.94 T against an ideal 6.09 T, about 65 %.
