implied_text: The condensate buffer is a connected superfluid volume. The superleak or film is apparatus that the normal fraction cannot pass — a spatial filter, not the condensate buffer. Quantized circulation requires a closed path.
description: Chargeless superflow needs connected 4He with ρs > 0; it does not need an electromagnetic screening depth.
notes: Vortex cores are the chargeless analog of mixed-state defects. Do not collapse this hardware with dilute alkali BECs.

observed_text: The attempt time τ0 is a fitted constant, usually taken as 1e-9–1e-10 s; values down to 1e-13 s are used. Measurement windows run from 1e-12 s (neutrons) through 1e-9–1e-7 s (Mössbauer) to about 100 s (dc magnetometry).
implied_text: Two clocks, and the effect is their ratio: the attempt time and the observer's window. Blocking is a statement about the observer as much as about the grain.
description: The failure clock is the Néel attempt time compared with the measurement window, not the 28 GHz/T precession carrier.
value_text: τ0 ~ 1e-9–1e-12 s; windows 1e-12 s to years
notes: The same grain can be blocked in one apparatus and unblocked in another.

observed_text: The effective anisotropy of a 5 nm magnetite particle from a Néel–Brown fit is 356 kJ/m³ against the bulk 13.5 kJ/m³. Surface anisotropy, interactions and coupling to neighbours sit between unit-cell anisotropy and the observed blocking temperature.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale Keff step.
description: The volume-and-time collapse does not depend on closing nanoparticle Keff; the mesoscale step remains underived.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Brownian relaxation in a fluid is a different machine and is not this entry.

observed_text: Holding the unblocked state costs no continuous power; the directional memory is simply gone. Zero continuous power on the blocked side as well.
implied_text: Neither the fluctuating unblocked ensemble nor the blocked parent latch draws hold power.
description: Holding either side of the blocking contour costs zero watts.

observed_text: On the unblocked side coercivity and remanence go to zero and M(H) is reversible, Langevin-like and scales with H/T. 4–5 nm magnetite: 294 Oe and 10.1 emu/g at 5 K against 12 Oe and zero at 300 K. Cooling or measuring faster restores the loop.
implied_text: Stable unblocked output is a zero-remanence ensemble curve plus the blocking surface, not a motor moment.
description: The unblocked grain emits a reversible Langevin curve and a blocking contour, not a usable remanent force.
notes: A single unblocked grain’s fluctuating moment is not a usable motor; the Langevin curve is already an ensemble average. Blocked side is the parent latch.

observed_text: Barrier ΔE = KV for uniaxial anisotropy and K1V/12 for cubic K1 < 0 (magnetite). Nd2Fe14B K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³; magnetite K1 = −1.35e4 J/m³. A 5 nm magnetite particle has an effective anisotropy of 356 kJ/m³, 26 times bulk. An antiferromagnetic matrix raises the blocking of 4 nm Co from 10 K to about 290 K.
implied_text: The barrier is a property of the grain and its surroundings together, not bulk K1 times volume.
description: The barrier that fails is KV, corrected for cubic symmetry, nanoparticle anisotropy and coupling to neighbours.
notes: The first version said the latch hardware is unchanged and only V differs. value_si is mid-range.

observed_text: τ = τ0 exp(KV/kT) against the measurement time: ln(τm/τ0) is 25.3 for 100 s, 40.3 for ten years and 2.3 for a Mössbauer window (τ0 = 1e-9 s). Recording media show decay onset at 35 ± 2 and need about 60 for ten-year storage. A 10 % change in diameter changes the retention time about four-thousand-fold.
implied_text: Thermal loss of direction on the observer's clock. Steep in size, with no critical value.
description: Small grains lose their direction on the observer's clock without reaching Tc.
value_text: KV ≈ kT ln(τm/τ0); 25 kT at 100 s
notes: The comparison with a thin-film mirror in the first version is withdrawn. The first version said 25 kT meant hours to years; it means about 100 s. T > Tc is the parent Curie threshold, not this crossover.

observed_text: KV = 25 kT at 300 K (100 s with τ0 = 1e-9 s): Nd2Fe14B (K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³) is a 3.4–3.6 nm sphere, volume 2.1–2.4e-26 m³; magnetite is 24.5 nm on K1 and 56 nm on the cubic barrier K1/12, and is reported at 20–50 nm. Tabulated: Fe 16 nm, Co 7 nm, Ni 34 nm.
implied_text: There is no minimum size. Retention time falls exponentially with the grain's barrier, and a size is quoted for a chosen waiting time.
description: The thermal-stability size of a magnetic grain is a few nanometres for Nd2Fe14B and tens of nanometres for magnetite at room temperature and 100 s.
notes: The first version gave ~30 nm for Nd2Fe14B and said magnetite was smaller; both were wrong. The Nd2Fe14B figure is computed here from sourced K1; no published table for it was opened. value_si is the Nd2Fe14B volume, mid-range.

observed_text: A surface plasmon resonance requires the real part of the metal permittivity to be negative and larger in magnitude than its imaginary part and the permittivity of the adjoining medium, which holds below the interband-screened edge of the metal.
implied_text: Optical-cycle synchronization of the same free-electron gas. Above the edge the bound mode no longer exists.
description: SPR shares reflection’s femtosecond screening clock; the new constraint is momentum, not a new cycle time.
notes: Cross-cite reflection:clock_latency:plasma-period and plasma-frequency-cutoff for the periods (0.28–1.1 fs). This file does not restate them.

observed_text: A momentum-matching coupler is required. The coupler is a wavevector match, not a buffer, clock, barrier, lattice, field threshold, or thermal limit.
implied_text: The load-bearing wavevector match does not sit in the six allowed constraint tags. The thickness window and the fill-fraction regimes are also not a single buffer number.
description: Tag-set gap plus a moving window: Medium mapping, not a contradiction of the electron-gas family.
value_text: k-match outside tag set; window and regimes, no floor
notes: File-level mapping remains Medium. Do not invent a seventh tag for one entry.

observed_text: A narrow dip appears in reflected intensity as angle or wavelength is scanned; the computed minimum is 0.6 % for 50 nm Au at 633 nm. The dip moves when the refractive index of the medium against the metal changes.
implied_text: A sharp angular or spectral absorption feature and a field bound to the interface, from synchronized oscillation of the metal electrons against the dielectric.
description: The stable output is the resonance dip and the interface-bound field, not a bulk mirror R.
notes: No universal minimum reflectance is quoted; the figure is for one film and wavelength.

observed_text: No stored state. The dip exists only while the film is driven through a coupler.
implied_text: No static barrier holds the dip. The mode exists only while it is driven.
description: SPR is a driven interface mode, not a stored directional state.

observed_text: The wavevector of the surface mode exceeds that of light in the adjoining dielectric, so a free-space photon cannot couple to it directly. A prism in attenuated total reflection (Kretschmann or Otto) or a grating supplies the difference.
implied_text: No in-plane momentum match → the interface mode is not launched → no dip.
description: Momentum match is load-bearing hardware and the primary collapse when the coupler or angle is absent.
value_text: no coupler, or θ / grating off the match
notes: total-internal-reflection supplies the prism evanescent field that Kretschmann and Otto use. Shared hardware, not a shared collapse.

observed_text: Computed minimum reflectance for Au at 633 nm goes from 6 % at 40 nm through 0.6 % at 50 nm to 15 % at 60 nm. In gold–dielectric composite films the dip is sharp above a metal fill fraction of about 0.6, very broad between about 0.4 and 0.6, and absent below about 0.4.
implied_text: Thickness off the window weakens the dip continuously. A granular film keeps a broadened dip until the metal fill falls below about 0.4.
description: Spatial failure is a window in thickness and a set of regimes in metal fill, both crossovers.
value_text: window about 45–55 nm (Au and Ag, 633 nm); fill fraction 0.4–0.6
notes: The first version listed a discontinuous morphology as killing the mode and compared the window with a 5–10 nm reflection cliff. The measured result is three regimes by fill fraction (Shi et al. 2009), and reflection has no such cliff.

observed_text: Computed from the single-interface dispersion relation with tabulated n and k at 450–633 nm: field 1/e depth 22–35 nm in the metal and 0.28–0.67 of a wavelength (176–423 nm) in air or water. Run along the surface at 633 nm: 65–73 µm on Ag–air, 25 µm on Ag–water, 9.8–15 µm on Au–air.
implied_text: The dielectric-side evanescent tail is an additional buffer. A coupler (prism index plus angle, or a grating period) is part of the hardware even though it is not the electron gas.
description: SPR occupies a sub-wavelength dielectric tail plus tens of nanometres of metal.
value_text: dielectric tail 0.3–0.7 λ; metal depth 22–35 nm
notes: Model values from measured optical constants; no direct measurement of a propagation length was opened. The run length is not the thickness window.

observed_text: Kretschmann measurements on 30, 52 and 70 nm gold found about 50 nm appropriate. Computed minimum p-polarised reflectance at 633 nm on a 1.515 prism: Au 6 % at 40 nm, 0.9 % at 45 nm, 0.6 % at 50 nm, 15 % at 60 nm; Ag 2.9 % at 50 nm, 1.0 % at 55 nm. Gold–dielectric composite films give the sharp dip only above a metal fill fraction of about 0.6 and no surface mode below about 0.4.
implied_text: Three spatial resources: a metal–dielectric interface, a thickness inside the coupler window, and enough metal in the plane. The window is not a universal 50 nm law.
description: SPR hardware is an interface, a thickness window and a metal fill fraction.
value_text: 45–55 nm (Au and Ag at 633 nm; Kretschmann window)
notes: The centre of the window moves with metal, wavelength and coupler (Au at 550 nm: near 40 nm). The first version contrasted this with a 10–20 nm mirror floor, which does not exist. Localized particle resonance is a different spatial resource.

observed_text: Carrier speed v is the long-wave acoustic slope. The transport clock is the scattering time τ = ℓ/v: boundary-limited and long at low T, umklapp-limited and short at high T. Zone-boundary / Debye periods remain the underlying oscillator clocks.
implied_text: Transport latency is ℓ/v, not the Debye period. No single τ is extracted.
description: The heat-current clock is the scattering time set by ℓ. Oscillator clocks stay with debye-cutoff.
notes: v owned by speed-of-sound; C(T) by debye-cutoff; this file owns ℓ. Kinetic-theory statement; no source opened for a scattering time.

observed_text: The mapping takes the kinetic formula and the Peierls umklapp distinction as descriptive data. It does not yet extract a particular ℓ(T) from node-level anharmonicity.
implied_text: The failing resource (ℓ) is identified; its value is not derived from node rules.
description: QSA names ℓ as the transport buffer but does not compute ℓ(T) from anharmonicity. Same unfinished anharmonicity as thermal-expansion.
value_text: κ = (1/3) C v ℓ taken; ℓ(T) underived
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Electronic thermal conductivity belongs with the electron population.

observed_text: Room temperature: natural diamond about 2200 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, isotopically pure about 3100. A 99.9 % ¹²C diamond reaches 41 000 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 104 K. Lattice part in metals: 2–18 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (Cu 17.6, Al 8.1, Ni 14.5).
implied_text: A material- and size-dependent κ(T) with the crystal peak-and-fall shape, produced by a synchronized phonon population limited by ℓ.
description: The transport machine emits a κ(T) set by heat capacity, sound speed and mean free path: thousands of W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ in diamond, 2–18 for the lattice part in metals.
value_text: diamond 2200–3100 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (300 K); lattice part in metals 2–18
notes: value_si is natural diamond at room temperature. The oxide-glass figure of about 1 W/m/K was removed: not sourced.

observed_text: No latched barrier. Umklapp is a kinematic threshold in the phonon population (enough large-q modes occupied) rather than an activation barrier that stores a state. T → 0 starves C; T → T_m removes the grid.
implied_text: The transport spec has occupation and grid conditions, not a memory barrier.
description: Phonon heat current is not a latch. Umklapp is kinematic; T → 0 or melting starve the channel.
value_text: umklapp kinematic; C→0 as T→0; grid to T_m

observed_text: Specimen size below the bulk ℓ makes κ follow the smallest dimension; with C ∝ T³ this gives κ ∝ T³ at low temperature in a clean insulator. Textbook statement; no source was opened and no measured scale is filed.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning of the path makes the sample the buffer. That is a size failure of the bulk-κ spec.
description: When L < intrinsic ℓ, the heat current is boundary-limited and κ tracks the specimen, not bulk umklapp.
value_text: L ≲ ℓ (Casimir); κ ∝ T³ at low T
notes: Any one peak temperature or residual ℓ is sample-dependent (medium).

observed_text: The crystal's phonon population ends at T_m. In a metal the conductivity drops sharply on melting and stays large because the electronic channel continues; the lattice contribution in liquid metals is about two orders of magnitude below the electronic one (tertiary source).
implied_text: Destroy the lattice and the crystal's phonon κ is gone. In a metal the measured κ is mostly electronic on both sides of T_m.
description: Melting ends the crystal's phonon heat current. A metal's measured κ drops and does not vanish.
value_text: T_m: lattice channel ends; a metal keeps its electronic κ
notes: Cross-cite melting and electron-heat-capacity. No opened source gives an insulator's κ across T_m.

observed_text: κ scales with ℓ. Natural diamond (1.07 % ¹³C) is about 2200 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at room temperature and an isotopically pure crystal about 3100. Glasses agree with one another within a factor of 5 from 0.05 to 100 K and show no crystal-like peak. In vitreous silica anharmonicity has a negligible effect on heat transport.
implied_text: ℓ is the load-bearing transport resource. Shorten it and the heat current dies even while the modes still exist.
description: The transport spec degrades as the mean free path shortens: isotopes, defects, disorder, and phonon–phonon scattering at high temperature.
value_text: ℓ set by isotopes, defects, disorder; diamond 2200 → 3100 W/m/K on isotope removal
notes: The 1/T umklapp law is a textbook statement and was not sourced.

observed_text: A lattice with propagating acoustic modes plus a mean free path: about 10⁻⁴ cm in glasses at 2 K, falling as T⁻⁴ at higher temperature; within 10 nm for phonons in metals at room temperature.
implied_text: Hardware is the phonon-carrying lattice plus the scattering length ℓ. When ℓ reaches the specimen size the specimen is the buffer.
description: Phonon κ requires a propagating lattice and an ℓ. Casimir makes the specimen the spatial buffer; a glass never provisions the crystal peak.
value_text: ℓ ~ 1 µm (glass, 2 K); < 10 nm (phonons in metals, 300 K)
notes: In metals phonons carry 1–40 % of the heat (Cu 4.7 %, Al 3.5 %, Ni 12.5 %).

observed_text: Exchange times are medium-specific: collision time 1.4e-10 s in ambient air (mean free path 64–68 nm over a mean speed of 471 m/s); electron–lattice energy transfer in a copper film 1–4 ps.
implied_text: Observation faster than the population’s exchange window returns a sequence of incomplete averages, not T.
description: The thermometer clock is the medium’s equilibration window; ordinary condensed samples have already finished on any mechanical or human clock.
notes: The earlier 'picoseconds to nanoseconds' for crystals was narrowed to the one opened measurement. Not a universal clock.

observed_text: k = 1.380649e-23 J/K is exact in SI. The N^{-1/2} scatter is the canonical-ensemble result and has been measured as temperature fluctuations. No universal minimum N exists.
implied_text: QSA takes the observed scatter and the measured equilibration time as buffer and clock. It does not derive k, or a minimum N, from node rules.
description: The statistical buffer is named as a class but not given a node-rule number. That is a gap, not a contradiction, and it recurs on every entry in this family.
value_text: k defined; no derived min N
notes: Treating the defined k as an extracted machine constant would over-claim.

observed_text: A body left in contact with a larger body, or isolated long enough, presents a single stable thermometer reading. Two bodies in contact converge; a third that matches the first matches the second.
implied_text: The stable product is one shared number T, and with it the conversion kT between that number and an energy scale.
description: T is the averaged output of the exchanging population, not a single-node property.
notes: k = 1.380649e-23 J/K is exact in SI, not an extracted machine constant. kT = 4.142e-21 J = 25.85 meV at 300 K is arithmetic from it.

observed_text: Equilibrium occupation follows the Boltzmann factor and equipartition gives ½kT per quadratic term; nothing in these relations is a barrier holding a state.
implied_text: T is produced by exchange among contributors, not by a barrier that protects a written state.
description: Temperature has no energy barrier that stores a state.
value_text: no latch; exchange, not a barrier
notes: Negative latch spec. Melting, superconductivity, and permanent-magnet-latch own the replacements.

observed_text: A reading taken inside the exchange window is not the equilibrium T; it approaches it on the exchange time (1.4e-10 s in air; 1–4 ps electron–lattice in copper).
implied_text: Drive or observation faster than the averaging window is a clock failure of the family: the output is not T.
description: Observe inside the exchange window and the thermometer does not report T.
notes: Crossover on the exchange time of the medium.

observed_text: With no exchange channel — no collisions, no radiation, no contact — two bodies do not converge to a shared reading.
implied_text: Zeroth-law contact is a resource. Isolation prevents a shared average.
description: Without an exchange channel the population cannot finish a common T.
notes: Zeroth-law statement; no number attached.

observed_text: Fractional energy scatter ~ N^{-1/2} (√(2/3N) for a monatomic gas). The reading degrades continuously as N falls. Isolation from a bath does not by itself forbid thermal local readings: an isolated quantum many-body system thermalizes locally while its full state stays pure.
implied_text: Fewer contributors mean larger scatter of the reading; the cut is the stability the instrument needs.
description: Under-populated averages fail gradually; there is no single N at which T switches off.
notes: Crossover; no N at which T switches off.

observed_text: Canonical energy variance is kT²C_V and the fractional fluctuation scales as N^{-1/2} (√(2/3N) for a monatomic ideal gas: 8 % at N = 100, 0.08 % at N = 1e6). Spontaneous temperature fluctuations have been measured and agree with the fluctuation–dissipation theorem.
implied_text: The hardware is a large exchanging population. Required N is set by the stability of the reading against the instrument, not by a material constant.
description: Temperature requires a statistical buffer; the scatter falls continuously as 1/√N with no node count marking a switch.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. No universal N.

observed_text: There is no separate expansion clock. The lattice clocks are the phonon spectrum; α(T) is the thermal occupation of those modes acting through γ. The laboratory length change follows the thermal equilibration time of the specimen, not an atomic period.
implied_text: α is an occupation readout of the existing phonon table, delayed only by specimen thermalization.
description: No dedicated expansion period is extracted. Laboratory ΔL follows thermal equilibration.
value_text: no separate clock; follows thermal equilibration
notes: Cross-cite phonon-dispersion and thermal-equilibrium-temperature.

observed_text: Anharmonicity is the stated condition and not a single hardware number. There is no measured threshold at which expansion turns on. QSA does not derive the 4.5–30 ×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ class from node-well shapes.
implied_text: The resource (anharmonicity) is named; its strength is taken as data. Invar shows that α ≈ 0 can also be a cancellation, which must not be misread as γ = 0.
description: Expansion is located as the anharmonic correction, but that resource is not pinned to one measured hardware number the way ω_p or T_m is.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Quasi-harmonic ω(q) shifts organize data and do not supply a single how-anharmonic number.

observed_text: Linear expansivity at 293 K, in 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹: W 4.5, Ti 8.6, Fe 11.8, Ni 13.4, Cu 16.5, Al 23.1, Zn 30.2.
implied_text: A small, material-typical α(T) as the averaged length change of an anharmonic, thermally occupied grid.
description: The expansion machine emits a material-typical α(T): 4.5–30 ×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ for the metals tabulated at 293 K.
notes: value_si left null: class, not one pin. Corrected from 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵.

observed_text: No latched barrier and no threshold number. The operating condition is anharmonic wells plus a finite temperature. There is no measured threshold at which expansion appears. No table of Grüneisen parameters was opened.
implied_text: Expansion is not a gated latch.
description: No activation barrier and no γ_c. Anharmonic wells plus finite T are the operating condition.
notes: γ → 0 is the harmonic-limit statement.

observed_text: A purely harmonic lattice would not expand: its mean spacing is independent of amplitude. This is a limiting condition on the wells and no material reaches it. Negative expansion exists (silicon −0.4, fused silica −0.53 ×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ at 100 K), so anharmonicity does not fix the sign.
implied_text: Remove anharmonicity and the length-change machine disappears, even though moduli, sound speed, and the 3N mode count remain.
description: The harmonic lattice does not expand. That is the named collapse of this effect.
notes: Harmonic statement is textbook, not sourced; the negative values are measured.

observed_text: Invar (64 Fe, 36 Ni): 1.4 at 100 K, 0.53 at 200 K, 0.13 at 293 K, 5.1 at 500 K and 17.1 at 800 K (10⁻⁶ K⁻¹); iron is 11.8 at 293 K. The low value is confined to a window near room temperature. The magnetic-volume explanation is cited and was not opened.
implied_text: α ≈ 0 without harmonic wells. That is not the harmonic-limit collapse.
description: Invar's near-zero α is a compensation confined to a temperature window, not harmonic wells.
value_text: Invar 0.13×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ at 293 K; 5.1 at 500 K
notes: Cross-cite magnetostriction (volume channel). Iron expands 91 times as much at 293 K.

observed_text: α falls toward zero at low temperature: copper 16.5 at 293 K and 10.3 at 100 K; diamond 1.0 and 0.05 (10⁻⁶ K⁻¹). It keeps rising with temperature up to melting: aluminium 12.2 at 100 K and 34.0 at 800 K.
implied_text: Starve C_V and expansion stops even if γ is finite. Melting ends the solid’s α spec; it is not an α cliff.
description: Low T kills α with the heat capacity. Melting ends the solid; α itself has no T_C-style pin.
value_text: α → 0 as T → 0 (Cu 16.5 → 10.3 at 100 K); rises to T_m
notes: Cross-cite debye-cutoff (C_V) and melting (high-T end of the same wells).

observed_text: A mechanically coupled lattice whose wells are not purely quadratic, large enough for a macroscopic length to be defined. If the restoring wells are purely quadratic, ⟨x⟩ is independent of T and α = 0. The harmonic grid that already produces speed-of-sound, elasticity, and debye-cutoff is not sufficient.
implied_text: Expansion is the anharmonic correction to the same ion-grid hardware. Harmonic springs provision moduli and a long-wave slope and still give α = 0.
description: The extra hardware is anharmonicity (γ ≠ 0), not a fourth reading of the harmonic springs.
value_text: γ ≠ 0 anharmonic wells; harmonic grid insufficient
notes: Invar adds a magnetic volume term. The harmonic-lattice statement is textbook and was not sourced. Anharmonicity does not fix the sign: Si and fused silica contract on heating at 100 K.

observed_text: Clock is the optical period. TIR works across the transparency window of the two dielectrics.
implied_text: Clock is not the load-bearing specification. The gate works wherever the two media are transparent and n1 > n2, and fails where the index contrast does — a failure of the underlying refraction machines.
description: TIR inherits the optical cycle of refraction; the collapse is geometric, not temporal.
notes: Cross-cite refraction-dielectric:clock_latency:optical-cycle (~2 fs visible) for the parent cycle time.

observed_text: The six allowed tags have no slot for angle or index contrast. spatial-buffer covers the interface, the evanescent tail, and frustrated-TIR starvation. It does not name the critical-angle gate.
implied_text: The θc / n1>n2 conditions are recorded as a geometry/contrast gate but are not a first-class constraint tag.
description: Limitation of the tag list, not a reason to invent a tag for one file. Mapping still rates High because two failure modes are sharp.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Not a new collective oscillator; kinematic gate on refraction’s n.

observed_text: Fresnel reflection coefficients have magnitude 1 (lossless media) for θ>θc, with an angle- and polarization-dependent phase.
implied_text: Unit reflectance for all θ>θc, together with a non-propagating field occupying a wavelength-scale volume on the far side.
description: The synchronized boundary response emits R=1 (lossless) and an evanescent occupancy, without a metal electron gas.
notes: Absorption in either medium → |r|<1 even above θc.

observed_text: Time-averaged Poynting flux through the interface is zero in lossless TIR. Energy still occupies the evanescent volume.
implied_text: Driven boundary response, not a latch. The word barrier for the low-index gap in frustrated TIR is a wave-tunneling metaphor, not an energy-barrier tag.
description: No stored state and no activation barrier. The gap is a spatial buffer.
value_text: no latch; evanescent gap is not ΔE

observed_text: θc = arcsin(n2/n1). Against air: glass (n1 = 1.50) 41.8°; water (1.333) 48.6°; polystyrene (1.49) 42.2°; diamond (2.42) 24.4°. For θ<θc a propagating transmitted beam appears and R<1.
implied_text: Incidence below the geometric gate → the total-reflection output is gone.
description: The load-bearing geometric collapse is θ<θc.
notes: value_si is 41.8° in radians, glass/air. Water 48.6°, diamond 24.4°. The condition is θ<θc, not a universal angle; it is sharp for a plane wave in lossless media. Metal reflection gives high R without any critical angle.

observed_text: A third medium brought within a few wavelengths of the surface receives a transmitted wave, and transmission rises as the gap narrows. No change in θ or in n1, n2 is needed.
implied_text: A third body in the 1/κ buffer takes light out of the reflected beam; the loss grows continuously as the gap narrows.
description: Frustrated TIR is a crossover in gap width, roughly e^(−2κg).
value_text: third body within ~1/κ (0.2 λ0 to a few λ0); continuous in gap
notes: surface-plasmon-resonance uses this tail as a coupler rather than as a collapse.

observed_text: No real θc exists if n1≤n2.
implied_text: Without index contrast the geometry gate never opens.
description: n1≤n2 is a binary contrast condition.
notes: Total internal reflection occurs only when the second medium has the lower index.

observed_text: An evanescent field occupies the low-index side. Amplitude decay length 1/κ = λ0 / (2π √(n1² sin²θ − n2²)), which diverges at θc. Glass/air (n1 = 1.50): 0.19 λ0 at 60°, 0.45 λ0 at 45°, 1.85 λ0 at 42°.
implied_text: An interface between two polarizable populations with n1>n2, plus a far-side buffer of order 1/κ. Same bound-charge machines as refraction-dielectric, not a new species.
description: TIR hardware is index contrast plus a wavelength-scale evanescent volume.
value_text: 1/κ ≈ 0.2 λ0 to a few λ0, diverging at θc
notes: A third medium inside the tail takes light out (frustrated TIR); that dependence on gap is continuous. Formula read on a tertiary page.

observed_text: Screening and core adjustment follow the parent-condensate electromagnetic / gap clocks (London / plasma scales; gap frequency). Flux-flow voltages, when present, sit on a much slower, geometry- and drive-dependent scale set by vortex velocity.
implied_text: This entry is not a voltage-standard clock; that lock lives on josephson-effect.
description: Mixed-state dynamics inherit the parent condensate clocks; flux flow is a slower, non-universal scale.
notes: Not the 483.6 MHz/μV lock.

observed_text: Pinning — the barrier that decides whether the mixed state is dissipationless — is set by microstructure (precipitates, grain boundaries, irradiation defects) and is not a universal function of λ and ξ.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale step. The Hc1 / Hc2 / κ collapses do not depend on closing it.
description: Mixed-state classification is closed; the pinning landscape that protects R=0 is still underived, of the same kind as mesoscale coercivity.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Same class of gap as permanent-magnet-latch coercivity. Superconductivity records the R=0 side of this gap.

observed_text: Between Hc1 and Hc2 flux enters as a triangular lattice of tubes, each carrying one flux quantum Φ0 = h/2e = 2.067 833 848…×10⁻¹⁵ Wb; the lattice is imaged by decorating a niobium surface with iron particles.
implied_text: A mixed state whose field scale is set by ξ and λ, whose flux is packaged as an integer number of Φ0 tubes, and whose lattice spacing is √(2Φ0/√3B), for as long as Hc1 < H < Hc2 and T < Tc.
description: The stable output is a field-tuned lattice of Φ0 phase defects.
notes: Same quantum as flux-quantization: a vortex is a phase defect that plays the role of the hole.

observed_text: Nb at 2 K: Bc1 ≈ 160 mT, Bc2 ≈ 300 mT. NbTi Bc2 = 14 T. YBCO films, extrapolated: 153 T and 638 T.
implied_text: Hc1 is the field threshold for first entry of a Φ0 defect. Hc2 is the field threshold that closes the gap. Pinning sites supply an additional barrier against vortex motion; that barrier protects the zero-resistance reading and is not the same threshold as Hc2.
description: The mixed-state window is the field interval between first vortex entry and gap closure.
value_text: Hc1 < H < Hc2 (Nb 0.16–0.30 T; NbTi to 14 T)
notes: NbTi and Nb3Sn remain superconducting in tesla-scale fields at liquid-helium temperature; YBCO does so at liquid-nitrogen temperature, with a strongly anisotropic Hc2. Specific tesla numbers live on superconductivity.

observed_text: Above Hc2 the cores overlap and the sample is normal: Nb ≈ 0.30 T at 2 K, NbTi 14 T.
implied_text: H > Hc2 destroys the ξ-buffer, closes the gap, and ends this artifact.
description: Upper-critical-field collapse is gap destruction, not first penetration.
notes: Collapse at Hc1 is a collapse of meissner, not of the gap. Treating them as one critical field would hide the vortex-lattice buffer.

observed_text: A transport current through an unpinned type-II conductor in a field moves the flux tubes and produces a flux-flow resistance; pinning centres prevent it. Pinned NbTi carries 3700 A/mm² at 5 T and 4.2 K.
implied_text: Free vortex motion is a failure of the R=0 artifact while the gap and the lattice are still present. That is a different collapse from Hc2.
description: Unpinned flux flow dumps dissipation into the mixed state without closing the gap.
notes: Owned jointly with superconductivity, which owns R=0. Pinning landscape is the consistency-gap row.

observed_text: Type II when κ = λ/ξ > 1/√2. From tabulated lengths: Al 0.010, Sn 0.22, Pb 0.44, Nb 2.8 (0.82 from a second table).
implied_text: Three nested spatial scales are required before this artifact exists as something other than a type-I Meissner state: ξ (core), λ (screening cloud), and the condition λ > ξ/√2.
description: Type II is the regime in which the screening cloud outruns the coherence-length core.
notes: λ is shared with meissner; ξ is the core size that closes at Hc2. This file owns the mixed-state window.

observed_text: The flux tubes form a triangular lattice with spacing √(2Φ0/√3B): 49 nm at 1 T and 20 nm at 6 T. Each tube carries one Φ0 and has a normal core of area about πξ².
implied_text: Vortex lattice spacing is an extra, field-tuned buffer that has no type-I counterpart. The mixed state is a synchronized array of these defects, not a uniform condensate.
description: At tesla-scale B the mixed-state lattice is a tens-of-nanometres array of Φ0 tubes.
value_text: d = √(2Φ0/√3B): 49 nm at 1 T, 20 nm at 6 T
notes: value_si is √(Φ0/1 T) from the stated Φ0. Spacing tracks the field; it is not a material constant.

observed_text: Attempt rates sit in the prefactor A T². The theoretical Richardson constant is 1.2017e6 A m⁻² K⁻² (120 A cm⁻² K⁻²). Vacuum transit is set by the anode voltage and the gap and belongs to collection. No opening time is filed.
implied_text: Collection latency is not the gate. A T² is the attempt-rate prefactor, not a stored-state cycle.
description: Opening φ is not a laboratory-scale clock. Transit belongs to collection.
value_text: A T² attempt prefactor; transit is collection
notes: A0 is a current-density prefactor, not a period. No opening-time number is given.

observed_text: QSA takes φ as a measured surface specification. It does not derive the 4.55 eV of tungsten from a more primitive node rule.
implied_text: No derivation of W's 4.55 eV from a surface-dipole plus chemical-potential construction. The thermal crossover in φ/kT does not depend on closing that derivation.
description: The gate is located and shown to be a surface resource; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step. A patchy surface is several gates read as one φ and one A.

observed_text: Richardson–Dushman J = A T² exp(−φ/kT). Theoretical A0 = 1.2017e6 A m⁻² K⁻². Apparent A is 60–100 A cm⁻² K⁻² for W, 60 for Ta and 55 for Mo, and 3.0 for thorium on tungsten, 40 times below A0. No illumination is required.
implied_text: Stable current density from a hot surface, with no optical drive, while surface, T, and collection field stay inside the envelope.
description: The machine’s stable product is a heat-opened surface current gated by φ.
notes: The first version said apparent A is of the same order as A0; that holds for clean metals and fails for coated cathodes. Apparent A is taken as a surface datum.

observed_text: Polycrystalline W 4.55 eV (4.54 eV in a second table); Cs 1.81–2.14 eV across compilations; thorium monolayer on W 2.63 eV. On clean outgassed W, Mo and Pd the thermionic and photoelectric work functions agree within 0.02–0.1 eV; on a composite surface they differ at low temperature.
implied_text: φ is the load-bearing gate. Heat opens it from below via the Boltzmann tail; a photon hν > φ opens the same gate from above. A surface field lowers it by 0.038 eV per square root of MV/m; it does not replace it.
description: Thermionic emission is the photoelectric-class surface gate opened by heat rather than by a photon. Not a latch; the electron leaves.
value_text: φ = 4.55 eV (W); Cs 1.81–2.14 eV; Th on W 2.63 eV
notes: value_si is polycrystalline W. W faces span 4.47–5.25 eV. The first version called the caesium range face-dependent; it is a spread between compilations. The primary compilations were not opened.

observed_text: J = A T² exp(−φ/kT). For W at 4.55 eV, φ/kT is 176 at 300 K (kT = 25.85 meV) and 21.1 at 2500 K; the Boltzmann factor is 3.7e-77 and 6.7e-10. φ/k is 5.28e4 K.
implied_text: Thermal emission falls continuously as exp(−φ/kT). There is no critical temperature; a cold cathode is dark because the factor is far below any instrument floor.
description: Emission is a continuous exponential in φ/kT. A cold tungsten part is not a cathode because the factor is of order 1e-77.
notes: The first version called this the collapse of the effect and a temperature cliff. The gate φ is sharp; its thermal opening is a crossover. The Richardson tail is thermal occupation of states above the barrier, not a second channel.

observed_text: The Richardson–Dushman law is a current per unit area, J = A T² exp(−φ/kT). A measurable cathode current is the summed output of the emitting area; reducing the area reduces the current in proportion.
implied_text: Emitting area is a capacity, not a second spatial cliff.
description: Macroscopic J is a rate of independent escapes. Area scales the current, not the on/off of φ.
notes: No minimum emitting area is extracted. Space charge (Child–Langmuir) is a collection ceiling, not this capacity.

observed_text: The conversion event is single-electron: one occupied state at the surface, one barrier φ, one escape. There is no collective coherence volume analogous to the mirror buffer of reflection.
implied_text: No collective buffer is required. One electron at a surface is the hardware. On a polycrystalline or coated surface the hardware is a set of patches, each with its own gate.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the heat-opened gate is single-particle. Contrast with reflection’s 10–20 nm stack.
notes: Photoelectric twin of the same surface φ. How to query effects that do not need a spatial buffer. No source was opened for this clause; it is the standard description.

observed_text: The X-ray period h/E is 4.1e-19 s at 10 keV. The 1.55 eV width of the copper K level corresponds to a core-hole lifetime of 0.42 fs.
implied_text: Conversion latency is the X-ray cycle. Hole lifetime is a smear of the same gate, not a second threshold.
description: Inner-shell conversion finishes on the X-ray cycle; eV-scale edge width is a clock smear of Eb.
value_text: 4.1×10⁻¹⁹ s at 10 keV; Cu K hole 0.42 fs

observed_text: QSA takes Eb from tables. It does not derive the 8.9789 keV of the copper K shell.
implied_text: No derivation of the keV class from node rules. The collapse hν < Eb does not depend on that derivation.

observed_text: At the Cu K edge μ/ρ goes from 38.29 to 278.4 cm² g⁻¹, a factor of 7.27. The position of the step identifies the element and the shell.
implied_text: An element-specific step in μ(E) at Eb^(s), reproducible enough to identify the element and, with finer structure, its local chemistry.
description: The machine’s stable product is a named-shell attenuation jump.
value_text: Cu K step at 8.9789 keV; μ/ρ 38.29 → 278.4 cm² g⁻¹ (×7.27)
notes: Fine structure above the edge comes from scattering of the photoelectron by neighbouring atoms. Tabulated edge shapes are an idealized sawtooth.

observed_text: Cu K edge at 8.9789 keV; Cu L1 edge at 1.0961 keV.
implied_text: Shell binding energies Eb^(K), Eb^(L), … are the operating gates — the same discrete energetic lock as φ and Eg, relocated to keV.
description: The X-ray absorption edge is a photoelectric-class inner-shell energy gate.
notes: value_si is Cu K. Edge position and shape are sensitive to valence and coordination; no shift size was sourced.

observed_text: Without the element there is no edge. No source was opened for an emptied shell.
implied_text: Missing hardware — no atom, or no occupied shell — closes that named gate.
description: The K-edge (or L-edge) is absent when the inner-shell node is not present.

observed_text: Below Eb that shell does not convert. At the Cu K edge μ/ρ goes from 38.29 to 278.4 cm² g⁻¹. The step is rounded by a 1.55 eV level width, 1.7e-4 of the edge energy.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of that shell’s conversion. That is the collapse of this edge.
description: Below the binding energy the named shell’s gate stays shut.
notes: Shallower shells and scattering still attenuate the beam. Pair production takes over at MeV energies.

observed_text: One atom with one occupied inner shell. Transmission is exp(−μt): thinning the sample reduces opacity in proportion and does not move the edge.
implied_text: No collective buffer. One occupied inner shell is the hardware.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the gate is single-particle.
